releases.title: More room for follow-up messages
changes: Long chats in shared assignments can now finish summarizing after a reply and reuse that summary on later turns.

releases.title: Smoother long conversations
changes: Long chats can reuse more history between tool steps. When Amplifier summarizes a finished turn, it aims to leave room for follow-up messages and can carry earlier saved progress into native compaction.
Open a working chat’s details to see its latest observed step.
This release also includes fixes to chat reading position, touch controls, and the privacy of appearance drafts.

releases.title: Simpler model controls for individual agents
changes: Choose a connection, model, and effort from the composer. In shared chats, choose the agent whose settings you want to change.
When a switch would make a long chat reread earlier messages, the picker can offer to keep the previous connection and model. It shows this option only when returning can avoid that extra work.
The settings popup takes less space. Click outside or press Escape to close it.

releases.title: Steadier chat lists while navigating
changes: Retain Browse and Status sidebar rows during chat switches and narrow-screen reopening, reducing loading-related row disappearance and layout shifts.

Retained rows do not count as fresh results: uncovered activity shows Updating, and stale Status paging stays disabled. Sign-in changes clear retained navigation state and prevent obsolete navigation owners from issuing new commands or updating the new navigation view.

releases.title: Model calls reappear when reopening older chats
changes: Reopening a long chat now restores saved model calls alongside tool calls, including their token usage and cost when available.
When only recent tool activity is available, Work details no longer reports a misleading zero model calls.

releases.title: Clearer suggested-message privacy settings
changes: The Privacy settings shortcut for suggested messages no longer describes the synced preference as a browser-only choice. It points to suggested messages, text sharing and provider charges in Chat & input.

releases.title: Grouped work and step details in chat
changes: Chat groups local work and updates from other chats. Expand a group to see what happened, then select a step to inspect it. Completed work stays grouped when you reopen the conversation.

Model calls show their outcome, provider, model, elapsed time, token and cache usage, and cost when available. If a diagnostic request or response was recorded and retained, you can open it separately.
The first turn that uses a different connection or model shows where the switch happened. You can see the potential impact of a pending change and restore the previous turn’s settings before sending.

releases.title: Suggested messages and clearer writing controls
changes: Optional suggested messages offer ideas for your next message, including in shared conversations. They start off, and your choice syncs across browsers connected to the same Amplifier installation, not across hosts or through a cloud account.

Choose a connection and model, with instructions and conversation-sharing options in Advanced settings. Suggestions send bounded displayed conversation text, including shared participants' messages, to that provider, not unsent drafts or private agent context. Provider charges may apply.

Press Tab or click a suggestion to place editable text in the composer, then send it separately. Nothing is sent as a chat message automatically. A saved suggestion can be reused while its conversation and settings remain unchanged.

Writing settings now distinguish Automatic, Send message and Start a new line. Automatic Return-key behavior is unchanged. Canvas keeps its main header toggle and removes the duplicate inner close button.

releases.title: Voice calls speak Amplifier's answers again
changes: Fix voice calls that said "I wasn't able to complete that request" for each request that needed Amplifier, while the answer appeared only in the chat. The voice now speaks the answer.
If a voice request does fail, the voice says in plain words whether Amplifier received it, and no longer passes on an internal error text. An answer that arrives after such a failure is still spoken.
A voice request made while an app update is being installed is declined with a plain message, instead of leaving the chat in an error state.

releases.title: Shared conversations and source-specific agent work
changes: Agents in shared ACP conversations can reply, use their existing tools, or stay silent in one turn. Participants that support attention requests can still decide whether to engage before taking a turn.

An ACP client and a configured Unified agent can now keep separate work for each source conversation, inspect whether an earlier input was received, and read, update, pause or stop that source’s work.
Peer reply receipts show the current outcome and retain earlier revisions. Newly queued ordinary peer messages can wait until the recipient is ready.
If the runtime cannot confirm a Stop request, the chat shows the outcome and keeps any reply the agent already finished.

notices.title: Shared-room messages can start a tool-using turn
notices.detail: An agent without an attention handshake can use its configured tools while deciding how to respond. Messages from other participants can also start a turn and incur model charges.
notices.action: When adding agents to a shared conversation, review their tool permissions. Use Stop to interrupt ongoing participation.

notices.title: Ordinary queued peer messages can arrive after a day
notices.detail: New ordinary peer messages wait without a default deadline. Existing deadlines still apply. Human resume requests and handoffs keep their one-day default.
notices.action: Set expiresInSeconds when a queued request will become stale.

releases.title: Keep chat messages safe when a turn starts during an update
changes: If an application update begins while a worker is preparing to send your message, Amplifier saves the message and sends it when the update finishes.
A new message that fails to start leaves the earlier turn and its outcome intact. You can retry the latest unsent message even when a background worker has since posted a report.
If an update interrupts an explicit retry, the message keeps its previous delivery status. Amplifier tells you when to retry and leaves that decision to you.

releases.title: Keep component updates working after a Git cache failure
changes: After a component update recovers from missing Git files, Amplifier remembers the cache that passed validation. Later updates using the same cache setting can install newer component revisions on the first attempt, including after Amplifier restarts.

releases.title: Recover component updates from a damaged download cache
changes: When a component update finds files missing from its local Git cache, Amplifier retries the update once with a fresh cache. Your installed components stay available while the new versions are prepared.

releases.title: Carry context across model and provider switches
changes: Change your selection as often as you like. The next message uses the final choice. When a change is known to require a large uncached request, a notice appears before you save it.

Compatible direct OpenAI and Anthropic models can reuse an existing native checkpoint. When switching providers, Amplifier keeps recent exchanges intact and uses a readable summary of earlier work when available.
Chats with interrupted preparation can continue on the selected model from saved progress. Previously confirmed work and the original conversation history are preserved.

releases.title: Private image diagnostics and image input for supported ChatGPT models
changes: ChatGPT connections can send supported PNG and JPEG images in user messages and matching tool results. Image support depends on the account route and selected model.
Claude chats preserve ordinary uploaded images and images returned by the tool that was called. Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM and OpenAI omit submitted image data from error diagnostics and retry reports.
Pinned image-capable models keep image support when the provider recommends a newer model.

releases.title: Faster OpenAI chats with image history
changes: Long OpenAI chats with images spend less time preparing diagnostics before a reply. Image data and private image URLs are omitted from diagnostic logs, including when an OpenAI error quotes an escaped URL.

releases.title: Let updates proceed past idle conversation recovery
changes: Component and Smart Tool updates no longer wait on idle conversations with failed settings changes. The conversations keep their saved settings and recovery records; updating does not resume or replay their work.
Keep active work protected during updates, including messages being sent while a conversation's worker starts.
Clarify how to change file-write permissions without replacing the conversation's full configuration.

releases.title: Resume interrupted preparation in the original chat
changes: If a model switch is interrupted after saving native preparation progress, Review preparation can let you pick up from the last completed step in the original chat.
The next send uses only the remaining preparation allowance. Unified keeps the saved conversation history and counts the unconfirmed call against the original allowance.
When saved preparation is blocked, chat diagnostics report the reason.

releases.title: Continue after a temporary conversation size-check failure
changes: If the selected connection cannot check a conversation's size, the chat now shows the counting diagnostic and what to do next.
For a temporary counting failure, Write a new message opens the composer in the original chat and keeps your draft. Sending remains your choice.

releases.title: Continue conversations paused during preparation
changes: When a saved conversation asks for a model choice, open the connection and model picker from the recovery message.

When a paused chat has eligible saved progress, review and approve an additional preparation allowance for the next message. If an earlier preparation call still has an unknown outcome, the recovery panel explains why more calls cannot be approved.
Settings makes Check for updates available again after a previous update process stopped during preparation, once Amplifier can verify that process exited.

releases.title: Approve a verified skill-cache move for one paused chat message
changes: A paused native model switch can offer a separate one-time choice when a worker update moved its skill cache. The recovery status control compares the named previous generation with the current generation and shows both identities when the saved request matches.

A new ordinary Send can approve that cache move and up to 32 additional preparation calls. The worker checks the source checkpoint, model, connection, tool configuration and both caches again. Existing progress counts toward the original allowance, and unused permission expires with the message.

notices.title: Continuing after a skill-cache move requires a separate choice
notices.detail: The worker will use the current generation’s skill cache for the acknowledged message. The comparison covers matching empty caches or identical empty lock files in qualified POSIX installations. Additional preparation calls can incur provider charges.
notices.action: Review the two generations and maximum additional calls before sending a new message with the cache-move acknowledgment.

releases.title: Keep component updates moving while a Smart Tool waits
changes: Amplifier can check and install worker components while a prepared Smart Tool waits for active work or a saved configuration operation to finish.
New workers can use the updated components while existing workers finish on their original version. Updates that require a restart still wait for a safe handoff.

releases.title: Continue paused native preparation with a one-time allowance
changes: Support one explicitly acknowledged continuation when a supported chat exhausts its native context-preparation allowance. A new ordinary Send can authorize an upper bound of 1-32 additional preparation calls; the default allowance remains 16.
Reuse the saved native summary prefix and confirmed preparation progress instead of starting over. Stop preparing once the saved prefix and remaining original messages fit the measured request.
Report additional calls authorized and used separately from the original allowance. Unused permission does not carry into another Send.
Keep portable summarization unchanged. Retries, scheduled work, peer messages and reopening or restarting a chat cannot authorize extra calls; existing Stop and uncertain-call protections remain.

notices.title: Continuing paused preparation can incur extra charges
notices.detail: An eligible native preparation that has exhausted its existing allowance can continue only with an explicitly acknowledged new ordinary Send and a one-time upper bound of 1-32 additional preparation calls. The default stays at 16. These are logical calls, not a limit on physical provider requests or an exactly-once billing guarantee. The permission applies only to that Send and does not extend portable summarization.
notices.action: Review the current offer and chosen additional-call limit before acknowledging the Send. Do not use Retry or a previous acknowledgment to approve more preparation. Changed Stop or model settings require a current valid offer, and uncertain calls must be reconciled rather than repeated.

releases.title: More reliable saved chats and app updates
changes: Fix a failure that could stop the next new message in a long saved chat after an update or model change.

Use the connection, model and reasoning options already confirmed for a local fork when sending its next new message after restart. Forks with only inherited settings still require an explicit choice.
Preserve prior failed inputs, unsent drafts and tool results during this continuation. Reopening a chat does not resend them.
Keep a saved chat's stopped, interrupted or error status when background startup prepares it for viewing.
Protect component source folders still referenced by saved chats during cleanup. This does not recreate sources already removed.
Before eligible Linux and macOS app updates, check that the existing prepared chat runtime can start and reopen a temporary chat. Keep the current app if the candidate introduces a startup failure.

releases.title: Switch models in existing chats with safer context preparation
changes: Continue supported existing chats after choosing a different connection or model. Amplifier prepares context for your choice when you send a new message, while preserving the original conversation history.

Avoid generating another summary when the original history already fits. When summarization is needed, retain confirmed progress and a cumulative call allowance across restarts, without automatically repeating uncertain calls.
Preserve compatible saved summaries when foreground context-fitting settings change. An unchanged full conversation fork can also retain a validated summary without making a model call.

Offer the supported reasoning-effort choices for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: low, medium, high, xhigh and max. Keep Provider default separate from an explicit choice rather than turning an inherited setting into a saved override.

Explain when model switching needs a Managed Context update or a compatible saved checkpoint. Recovery requested immediately after startup now checks the saved checkpoint before recording a new recovery attempt.

Keep usable text chats and ordinary tools available when an unavailable provider or an older tool prevents file-image support from being verified. Unverified image reads remain unavailable rather than bypassing the image checks.

notices.title: Changing models can require additional paid preparation
notices.detail: Choosing a connection or model does not itself make a model call. Your next new message can start preparation for that choice, including paid summarization. Preparation shares one cumulative summary-call allowance, 16 by default, across restarts and supported continuations. This limits logical calls, not physical requests or exactly-once billing. Changed defaults, scheduled work and retries do not start a new paid model transition.
notices.action: Choose the connection and model explicitly, then send a new message. If an older chat runtime reports that switching is unsupported, select the previous connection and model, or update Managed Context in Settings and send again. Returning to the previous model requires its saved state still to validate. Do not repeat an uncertain action or use recovery to bypass a rejected checkpoint.

notices.title: Keep a backup before returning to an older version
notices.detail: New-format compaction checkpoints, including partially completed summaries, are rejected by the standard Unified 0.111.4 configuration. An unchanged checkpoint imported from that version remains reusable with its original model, history and settings. Original messages remain available; reading a rejected checkpoint makes no model call, but later summarization can incur new charges.
notices.action: Before upgrading, let active work settle and back up conversation history, checkpoints, settings and operation records together. Before downgrading, preserve newer work separately and use a copy of the pre-upgrade backup. Reconcile actions completed since that backup before resuming them.

notices.title: A continuing text chat may not have access to saved images
notices.detail: File-image support remains disabled when startup cannot verify it because a provider is unavailable or an older tool registers outside the supported image path. OpenAI's native compacted context can also prevent saved-image projection, including after a model change. Saved image references remain, but the model receives an Image unavailable warning rather than those pixels. This is separate from supported fresh inline attachments.
notices.action: Do not assume a successful text answer means the model saw the saved images. Continue only work that does not need them, or use a separately supported image workflow.

releases.title: Read image files in conversations
changes: In supported sessions, Amplifier can read an authorized local image with read_file and send it as an image to a compatible model. File permissions still apply, and supported formats depend on the selected provider and model.
Composer images stay available when switching between compatible providers. An unreadable attachment no longer prevents the rest of the message from being sent.
Image payloads are omitted from provider diagnostic captures. Admitted composer images are still retained in saved conversation history.

releases.title: Update runtime components on older installations
changes: Older installations can update runtime components again when Amplifier verifies which branch each component follows.
Components you pinned keep their chosen revisions, including dependencies used by another component.

releases.title: More reliable long chats and updates
changes: Prepare a measured request for supported long chats before waiting for optional conversation summaries. When needed, try a smaller complete view while retaining required inputs and unresolved-operation information.

Let oversized completed tool outputs use references to their exact saved results, while keeping the tool calls and result identities together. Full results remain in history; retrieving them does not require running the tools again.

Prepare optional checkpoints after eligible completed turns without replacing the conversation's foreground activity status. New foreground work or Stop cancels this maintenance, and stale results cannot replace the current checkpoint.
Match edited messages to their original submissions more accurately when a conversation contains repeated text.

Let a newer application update proceed while a Smart Tool with a known staged target waits to activate. The tool keeps its own activation conditions and failure receipts; application replacement still waits for an idle host.
Give macOS updater subprocesses more room to open files while resolving dependencies, within the operating system's limit.

notices.title: Long chats can answer before their next summary
notices.detail: Supported Boundary chats now fit the current request before optional compaction by default. A request can omit earlier settled exchanges or replace a large completed tool output with a reference to its saved original. Full history remains saved. Optional checkpoint preparation can run after an eligible completed turn and may use the configured model after the answer appears. Explicit context settings remain respected.
notices.action: If earlier evidence matters, inspect saved history and the referenced results and provide the relevant details again. Do not repeat an action just because its full result is absent from the current request. Advanced configurations can retain foreground compaction with compaction_schedule: foreground. This change does not recover previously blocked conversations or settle uncertain operations.

releases.title: More reliable context preparation and message editing
changes: Keep ordinary turns stable when a background job returns during context preparation or an idle conversation changes models.

When an optional full-history size check has a transient failure, try a smaller request while still requiring an authoritative size check before sending it. Avoid repeating an unchanged optional compaction preflight that was already rejected as too large.
Replace an optional context-preparation failure status with Thinking once an ordinary model request is admitted, without hiding real terminal failures.
Avoid copying unrelated execution and draft state into message-edit commands. Required message content, saved history, revision checks and the 48 MB transport limit remain intact.

releases.title: Independent publishing, transfer and extension packages
changes: Package maintenance: Shell SDK, Publishing and Portability now come from their independently published packages. Existing web behavior, saved state and recovery are preserved.

releases.title: Continue long chats with clear context warnings
changes: Let supported Boundary chats continue when optional compaction fails or is deferred, by fitting complete settled exchanges within the selected model's allowance. Saved history is preserved.
Show a quiet, dismissible notice when a foreground request is dispatched with earlier context omitted. Dismissing the notice does not restore that context.
Keep uncertain recovery candidates and checkpoints separate from ordinary continuation, without automatically retrying or committing them.

notices.title: Long chats can continue without all earlier context
notices.detail: Unified now enables request fitting by default for supported Boundary contexts unless explicitly disabled. When optional compaction cannot complete or is deferred, a request can omit whole settled exchanges, including completed tool exchanges from the current turn, without summarizing them. The omitted exchanges remain in saved history. The request retains required current inputs, instructions and unresolved-operation information; it still stops if required content cannot fit. The model receives an incomplete-context warning, and the conversation shows a dismissible notice when a degraded foreground request is dispatched.
notices.action: If earlier evidence matters, inspect saved history and receipts and provide the relevant details again. Do not repeat an action merely because its evidence is absent from the current request. Dismissing the notice does not restore context, repair a checkpoint or settle an uncertain operation. This release does not establish recovery of previously blocked conversations.

releases.title: Component updates finish again, and clearer Updates and Windows setup messages
changes: Let component updates finish again on installations with an OpenAI API connection; in 0.108.0 and 0.109.0 such an update could stop for a source review and stay offered.
Remove the copies of the app's sign-in secrets and TLS private key that earlier versions left in component-update folders. This runs by itself while Amplifier is idle and can take several passes.

Fix several cases where the Updates page said that an update could not finish, or that component verification was incomplete, although nothing had failed, such as after saving an AI connection or after Amplifier restarts.
Send one tool definition with "Send test message", accept an answer that is only a tool call, and say plainly when a connection cannot send a test message.
Keep a new browser tab from opening the first-use panel again after your first chat or a finished setup.
When Windows setup runs again, say only what setup found, and do not start Amplifier in a folder that holds an unfinished uninstall.

Pause the support for images returned by the file-reading tool in OpenAI chats, which 0.108.0 added on Linux and macOS: after a component update the model does not receive those images until the app's reviewed file list matches the OpenAI component again. Chats and file reading keep working.
Package maintenance: Status updates and the Python and JavaScript execution kernels now come from their independently published packages. Existing behavior and saved work are preserved.

notices.title: OpenAI file-tool images may be unavailable after a component update
notices.detail: The default OpenAI provider follows its standard update branch again, allowing component updates to finish. On Linux and macOS, images returned by file-reading tools are available only while the selected provider matches the app's reviewed image support; an update can disable that support. Explicitly configured provider sources are preserved. This image route remains unavailable on Windows.
notices.action: Check image support before relying on analysis of images returned by file-reading tools. Text chats and file reading remain available.

notices.title: Old credential copies in update folders are removed automatically
notices.detail: While Amplifier is idle, maintenance removes obsolete configuration and routing copies from component-update folders, including copies that contain sign-in secrets and the TLS private key. Cleanup may need several passes and leaves the active configuration in place.
notices.action: No manual cleanup is needed. Keep backups separately from temporary update folders. This cleanup is best-effort deletion, not secure erasure.

releases.title: Separate decision connections from chat providers
changes: Keep recognized browser and computer decision-service connections separate from chat-model providers, while continuing to manage both in AI connections & decision models.
Let Windows setup recreate missing Start-menu and Apps-list entries when run again after an uninstall leaves an eligible private Start-menu folder, leaving files with other names in place.

notices.title: Decision connections move to separate settings
notices.detail: On startup, and when saving connection or decision-model settings, Unified can move recognized decision-service declarations into a separate section of the same settings file. Unrelated preference saves do not migrate accounts. Global and participating workspace files are updated individually, not as one transaction; existing session settings are not swept. Chat-account credentials remain with their chat account. Unknown, unavailable or ambiguous adapter metadata, or unresolved conflicts, can leave legacy declarations in place, where they may still affect the CLI. Older Unified versions may not read the migrated decision configuration.
notices.action: Normally no manual move is needed. If migration or saving reports an error, preserve the affected files and error for troubleshooting rather than deleting or recreating accounts. If you may need to return to an older Unified version, keep a private pre-update copy of the affected settings before first running updated Unified; this migration does not provide an automatic downgrade conversion. Start a new conversation after changing decision preferences; existing runtime plans are not rewritten.

releases.title: Images from file-reading tools and more reliable updates
changes: Let supported OpenAI chats use PNG and JPEG images returned by the file-reading tool during ordinary streaming Work. Other providers, tools and nested or blocking Work are not newly qualified by this release.
On managed Windows installations, automatically repair a specific compiled-cache problem left by older versions that could prevent connections or component updates from starting.
Stop copying the app's sign-in secrets and TLS private key into newly prepared component-update folders. Earlier copies are not removed by this change.
Keep bounded, private explanations of future installer failures on this computer, including both attempts when an eligible retry occurs.
Keep Windows pages responsive while an updated app confirms its startup with Task Scheduler.
Improve Windows uninstall guidance and allow brief waits for a slow activity check or a temporarily held Start-menu shortcut before stopping the uninstall.

When Windows setup cannot find the launcher in a leftover installation folder, but finds a recorded choice to delete data and no chats or settings, it now tells you to move or rename the folder before trying setup again. Setup does not change or delete the folder.

notices.title: OpenAI's fallback provider source is now fixed
notices.detail: When no explicit provider source is selected, Unified's OpenAI catalog fallback now uses the reviewed revision included with this release instead of following the latest main branch. This can also affect existing connections that rely on that fallback. Explicit source choices and disabled connections remain respected; saved models and credentials are not rewritten.
notices.action: No configuration change is needed to use the release default. If you intentionally track main or another revision, keep or set an explicit provider source. This notice does not restart a running conversation or replace its runtime.

notices.title: Windows startup can repair older component caches
notices.detail: Managed Windows installations now check for a specific compiled-cache problem left by older versions. At startup, Amplifier can remove untracked compiled Python cache files when the cached component otherwise passes its checks. Unexpected changes and links are left alone. These checks use Git, which can run programs configured for its filters.
notices.action: Allow the startup check to finish. No manual cache removal is required for this repair. If the connection still fails, keep the current error for troubleshooting rather than deleting your chats or installation data.

notices.title: Review update files before sharing them
notices.detail: Future failed update commands can save small, private installer-error excerpts on this computer. Redaction is best effort; the excerpts are not automatically included in support reports, feedback or shared diagnostics. New update folders no longer copy the app's private configuration folder, but older folders can still contain sign-in material and TLS keys. Temporary qualification credentials can also remain after an interrupted preparation.
notices.action: Review excerpts locally before sharing them, and do not send an entire update folder as a support attachment. amplifier-unified doctor --verbose shows the local explanation folder without printing its contents. This release does not clean private copies from older update folders.

releases.title: Adaptive Canvas navigation and fresher chat status
changes: Choose Auto, Tabs or Compact navigation in Canvas. Auto is the default and adapts to the panel's size; explicit choices stay in this browser. Find full document titles and close documents from the list. A tighter toolbar places Copy and Refresh in Details while layout changes preserve open viewers and unsaved edits.

Keep retained Pinned and Recent chat rows, and already-open Chat details, aligned with current activity. Show a neutral Updating status when current activity is unavailable, while preserving pending-answer and unconfirmed answer-delivery warnings and saved history.

Improve Windows browser-entry refusal guidance: suggest the Start menu only when the host verifies the required local installation conditions, otherwise give a generic next step. The open command's failure messages no longer recommend running that same command again.
Avoid repeatedly revalidating a prepared component update after validation fails. Automatic retry waits for changed update inputs or an app restart; you can use Try update again to retry explicitly.
On supported Windows installations, update the launcher automatically when an app update requires it, and show the confirmed app version in Windows Apps.
Allow more time for the decision-catalog helper to start in a new chat environment, avoiding premature startup failures on slower starts. A helper that hangs still has a two-minute limit.

notices.title: Windows launcher updates can cause an additional restart
notices.detail: With Keep Amplifier up to date enabled, supported Windows installations can now replace the launcher after a confirmed app update when launcher files differ. This uses a same-account scheduled helper and waits for work to finish before restarting Amplifier again. Failed replacement attempts restore the earlier launcher where recovery succeeds; incomplete recovery can need manual intervention. The first automatic refresh retains the previous launcher; later successful refreshes may remove older launcher backups created by this mechanism.
notices.action: Allow the extra restart to finish. To defer future automatic launcher updates, turn off Keep Amplifier up to date before a refresh starts. This does not cancel recovery of a refresh already underway. Use Retry installation when offered on the Updates page. If Amplifier does not return, recovery may require a terminal; the Updates page cannot guide recovery while the app is down.

releases.title: Daily changelog groups and cleaner app icons
changes: Group the Changelog by recorded UTC dates and show how many listed releases belong to each day. Releases with unknown dates remain under Undated; installed notes stay available offline.
Show the original Amplifier mark directly on rounded app icons, without the added rim or logo halo. Existing appearance accents, fixed colors and uploaded icons remain supported.

Remove temporary connection-key copies when a chat-specific setup fails or is stopped. If removal is refused, idle maintenance retries unvalidated stages only when the saved attempt record says failed or cancelled; unvalidated stages still marked preparing remain protected. Stage folders, settings, routing and live credentials are retained.

releases.title: Clearer updates and safer connection checks
changes: Updates distinguish installation from waiting for running work, and retry checks component sources again.
Completed component update stages remove their temporary copy of connection keys.
Connection checks avoid changing stored provider source files, including on Windows.
Recall storage now comes from its independently published package, preserving saved notes, versions and recovery history.

releases.title: Output maintenance
changes: Output relationships and Git review now use their independently published package, while preserving saved outputs and local review history.

releases.title: Windows startup, setup and update repairs
changes: Improve Windows launcher startup feedback, avoid duplicate browser tabs during one start, and wait for commands handed to the active app so their output and exit status are returned correctly.

Record certificates replaced by setup-tls force for remote access. Updated launchers can ask Windows to remove those recorded earlier certificates after you accept the new certificate, and during uninstall. Older certificates that were never recorded are left untouched.

Allow Windows chat-specific setups to prepare with long paths disabled, and explain when a chosen folder path is too long before creating the chat. This does not rename existing chat history or remove the documented helper and background-job path limits.
Check for updates once soon after startup when the previous check or attempt is at least one hour old, while retaining the four-hour timed interval and existing automatic-update admission rules.

Avoid reporting unfetched first-use components as updates on a new installation, and avoid an unnecessary component refresh after its first chat. A new installation without an AI connection can show up to date when no real update was found; component installation still waits for a connection.
Improve server-provided remote sign-in guidance and keep the Sign in controls nearer the top of small windows.
Use the independently published Worktrees package with its exact paired Portability artifact, preserving existing runtime behavior, ownership records and transfer history.
Verify before publication that Windows setup uses the Git component revisions recorded by that release's host and runtime checks.

notices.title: Windows launcher improvements need the updated launcher
notices.detail: An app update does not replace an existing Windows launcher. Startup feedback, command handoff and recorded-certificate removal at open or uninstall require a newer setup installation or the supported launcher refresh. Certificate removal still asks Windows for your approval, and cannot identify older certificates that were never recorded.
notices.action: Use the supported launcher refresh when updating an existing installation. Review each certificate prompt; do not remove certificates by their display name.

notices.title: Automatic update checks also run after startup
notices.detail: When automatic checks are enabled, startup can check once if the last check or attempt was at least one hour ago. With Keep Amplifier up to date enabled, an eligible update can follow through normal admission without interrupting running work. A failed startup check waits until the next automatic interval; a waiting update sequence's component check can consume the startup check.
notices.action: Use Check for updates for an immediate manual check, or adjust the existing automatic-check and update settings if you prefer manual updates.

notices.title: Known issue with OpenAI-compatible connections
notices.detail: On Windows, saving an OpenAI Compatible API connection can leave generated bytecode in a shared source object, preventing its chats from starting and causing later component checks to fail. This release does not include prevention or repair of already affected source objects; other platforms have not been qualified for this finding.
notices.action: Avoid adding this connection type until its repair is released. If already affected, keep the diagnostic details and use the supported repair guidance when available; this release does not clean or migrate the source store.

releases.title: Operation tracking and provider file maintenance
changes: Operation tracking now uses its independently published package, while preserving existing work and recovery history.
Anthropic’s default rate-limit and optional fallback files now stay in the app’s shared data folder, including within a Windows installation. Explicitly configured file paths are preserved.

notices.title: Anthropic state follows the app’s data folder
notices.detail: If your shared Amplifier home differs from ~/.amplifier, Anthropic’s default rate-limit and optional fallback files now use that folder. They no longer implicitly share state with runtimes using ~/.amplifier. Existing files are left in place, and paths you explicitly configured stay unchanged.
notices.action: If you intentionally share this state with another runtime, configure explicit provider file paths. No file cleanup or migration is performed automatically.

releases.title: Appearance-aware app icons and clearer context recovery
changes: Let default app icons follow each browser’s confirmed appearance accent, with rounded badges and contrasting marks. Fixed icon colors and uploaded images remain supported; Reset in App name & icon restores the appearance-based default.
Keep icon colors current when switching app surfaces or confirming appearance changes, without applying an unconfirmed appearance preview to the saved app icon.

Preserve compatible saved summary progress when conversation preparation reaches its call allowance, including when newer messages have arrived. Incompatible progress stops before replacement summary work; another preparation requires separate admission and may still fail to fit the remaining context.

Bound transcript-search output even when the first matching turn is unusually large. A partial-result notice explains omitted content; canonical history is preserved. This prevents new oversized retrieval results but does not automatically repair an oversized result already saved in a chat.

Keep the distinct preparation-pause and incompatible-progress reasons visible through the app, without automatic retry or exposing private error content. Complete the normal component update to use the accepted Context and loop-live repairs; app installation alone is not proof that a running chat has adopted them.

notices.title: Default app icons now follow appearance
notices.detail: When no fixed icon color or uploaded image is selected, the app icon uses the confirmed appearance accent rather than a listener-derived color. The same service can therefore have different default icon colors in different browsers or color schemes. Existing explicit colors and uploads are preserved.
notices.action: Choose a fixed color in App name & icon if you want the same color across browsers. Reset restores the appearance-based default. Installed operating-system icons may refresh separately from the browser; this release does not claim that every installed shortcut updates immediately.

releases.title: Apply selected component versions
changes: When you select a different exact commit for a module from the same repository, Update now prepares that selection instead of retaining the old commit and stopping preparation.
The previous working generation and rollback records remain intact; conflicting source declarations or changed preparation inputs still stop the update safely.
Unified now selects the published Workspace Metadata package and retires its duplicate source and release tooling, preserving the existing runtime behavior.
Documentation clarifies the supported ACP pilot compositions and their remaining compatibility and qualification limits.

releases.title: Stronger tool-approval matching and Windows uninstall choices
changes: Bind remembered Bash approvals to the effective environment, safety configuration and execution limits. Supported stdio MCP approvals also identify the opened connection, connected tool schema and arguments; unsupported execution forms retain one-time approval.

Support exact HTTP MCP approval matching with compatible components that recheck authorization when sending the request. Older components and custom HTTP authentication remain one-time approvals. Existing approval modes, budgets and uncertain-operation protections remain unchanged; this release does not enable Automatic.

Add an optional Windows uninstall choice to delete installation-owned data and program files after two explicit Yes answers. The default keeps the folder, and unrecognized top-level entries remain. Existing installations receive launcher changes only through the supported launcher refresh.

Report compaction progress as saved parts and pending segments that may split further, without a fixed total, percentage or estimated completion time. An empty summary queue no longer implies that preparation has finished. This reporting change does not itself accelerate compaction or recover failed conversations.
Clarify Windows 11 preview setup instructions for Microsoft Edge, file locations, account, path and certificate stops, and the keep-or-delete uninstall choices.

notices.title: Windows uninstall can now delete saved data
notices.detail: When the updated launcher offers the delete choice, the first question defaults to No: uninstall and keep the whole folder. Choosing Yes twice permits permanent deletion of chats, settings, saved accounts, stored keys, workspace files and program files in the installation. Unrecognized top-level entries remain; files inside recognized data and workspace folders are within the deletion scope. Cancel, or No at the second question, does not begin deletion.
notices.action: Back up anything you want to keep outside the installation folder before choosing deletion. If removal cannot finish, follow its Uninstall guidance; Amplifier remains unavailable while removal is unfinished. An app update alone does not replace an older launcher: use the supported launcher refresh. Some older installations retain the original keep-folder question.

notices.title: Remembered approvals require matching execution facts
notices.detail: Supported Bash and MCP requests now use more specific execution and connection facts. Requests that do not match a remembered rule ask again; unverifiable tools, unsupported shell operations and custom HTTP authentication remain one-time approvals. Automatic remains a separate explicit choice. A matching rule never permits replay of an uncertain prior operation.
notices.action: Complete the normal component update where needed and review the exact request before choosing Always. Do not infer running component support from the application version alone. Choose one-time approval when you intend to approve only the current request.

releases.title: Retire the legacy native-client adapter
changes: Remove the temporary /api/companion compatibility API after the maintained native clients moved to generic observations for conversation, attention and activity views.

Preserve existing service registrations, credentials, preferences and reply identities. Native credentials retain their restricted observation and presentation permissions; this change does not grant general command access.
Keep observation display preparation within a single request while removing the obsolete adapter and its authentication branch. Existing authority, isolation and revocation checks remain in place.

notices.title: Upgrade older native clients before updating services
notices.detail: This release removes /api/companion. Older native clients or custom consumers that still use that API will no longer work with an updated service. The maintained native clients now use generic observations; existing credentials and saved service identities are preserved.
notices.action: Before adopting this service update, upgrade every connected native client to a release that supports generic observations. Move custom consumers to the documented observation APIs; do not rely on the removed compatibility route.

releases.title: Reliable Windows state reads and preview setup guidance
changes: Windows private-state readers now reopen and revalidate a file when another Amplifier process replaces it during a read. This avoids false failure messages during Stop, status, startup and update handling while preserving private-file checks.
The README now links to the Windows 11 preview setup file and explains download warnings, first start and the current uninstall behavior.

notices.title: Existing Windows launchers need a separate refresh
notices.detail: An in-app update installs the app-side repair but does not replace the installed Windows launcher. Stop Amplifier, launcher status and uninstall use that launcher's code. Those launcher paths receive this fix through the new setup file or the supported launcher refresh command.
notices.action: For an existing Windows installation, use the supported launcher refresh procedure to update its launcher; do not treat the in-app update alone as installing this launcher fix.

releases.title: Give each Amplifier app its own name and icon
changes: Settings now offers App name & icon for this server. Rename the app, choose its badge color, or upload an image with preview and reset controls.
Default names include the server computer name and its nonstandard port, helping distinguish installations. Choices are shared by browsers connected to that listener and survive restart.

App titles, headers, install metadata and icons follow the saved choices without changing the app URL or installed identity. Icon uploads are sanitized and sized for private storage; oversized settings leave the saved state unchanged.

notices.title: App names and icons now identify the server
notices.detail: The default app name and badge change to identify this server. Customize them in Settings → App name & icon. Browsers decide when an existing installed app refreshes its name and icon; this does not require a new app identity or a reinstall.
notices.action: Use Settings → App name & icon to choose the name and icon you want.

releases.title: Shared update dismissals for native clients
changes: Add bounded general observation access for existing approved native-client credentials, with explicit service identity and shared display-dismissal receipts. These credentials do not gain general command or browser-control authority.

Supporting native clients can dismiss an update's exact observed state across approved devices connected to the same service account. Dismissal does not mark it read, resolve attention, stop work or approve an action, and a new response or action remains visible. Separate service installations remain separate authorities.

Provide bounded plain-text activity hints from current execution projections without loading full conversation history or exposing raw tool inputs and results. Keep paged observation and dismissal views consistent.

Retain the legacy native-client feed during the coordinated service and client transition. This release does not remove that adapter, deliver new Mac or Windows apps, or perform live service adoption.

notices.title: Update every registered service before switching native clients
notices.detail: The new shared-dismissal contract is additive. Independently shipped native clients must discover observations.identity and dismissals.version 1 on every registered service before switching to it. Installing this application release does not by itself update native apps or prove that all services adopted the capability. Existing native clients can continue using the retained legacy feed during the transition.
notices.action: Complete the ordered service updates and confirm both advertised capabilities on every registered service before activating the Mac or Windows client successor. Keep the legacy adapter until the native cutover is verified; do not infer readiness from the app version alone.

releases.title: Use the public Scheduling package
changes: Select the published Scheduling 0.1.0 artifact from its standalone public repository and retire Unified's temporary Scheduling authoring copy. The bundled runtime, license and runtime requirements are unchanged; Unified remains the sole installed distribution owner.

Update Scheduling ownership and artifact-selection guidance. The remaining shared package workflow publishes Status only; historical Scheduling receipts remain verifiable. No scheduling behavior, approval mode or live installation is changed by this packaging update.

releases.title: Repair component updates and prepare exact approval support
changes: Fix component updates that could stop when an app-managed dependency such as Memory was recorded as an unresolved fixed revision. Verify its configured branch before preparing a new generation, while preserving explicit pins, forks, other source choices and existing runtime records.

Add Unified-side support for exact native-tool approval descriptions used by supporting Instances. Matching describes the selected tool, arguments, working folder and applicable policy. Cross-chat native-tool Always remains unavailable on the currently accepted streaming component; activation requires a compatible accepted component and normal component update.

Existing approval modes remain unchanged. Remembered approval support applies only to future new matching requests; this release does not enable Automatic, retry uncertain operations or recover blocked conversations. The Fable counting and summary repairs published in 0.101.1 remain included, but app installation alone does not prove that an existing worker adopted them.

Correct Windows file-timestamp comparisons used to verify selected tool packages, avoiding false rejection when path and open-file metadata expose different clocks. Changed-file and source checks remain enforced; native Windows behavior was not newly verified.
Allow the existing Scheduling artifact-selection workflow to recognize explicitly identified standalone Scheduling receipts; selected component artifacts and runtime behavior are unchanged.

Clarify native Full access: supported file tools can access files outside the workspace and configured allowed or blocked folders wherever the operating-system account permits. Ask when needed restores the configured restrictions. This is a disclosure correction, not a permission-policy change; the separate external-agent explanation is unchanged.

notices.title: Native-tool Always needs a compatible component
notices.detail: This release adds Unified-side support only. The current accepted streaming component retains ordinary one-time native-tool approvals. An app update alone does not enable cross-chat native-tool Always or Automatic. On a compatible supporting Instance, an Always choice can apply to future exact matching requests in other chats for that agent, not to uncertain prior operations.
notices.action: Continue using one-time approval on the current component. If a compatible component is subsequently accepted and made available, use the normal component-update flow; do not select an unmerged source. Review the exact request and displayed scope before choosing Always.

releases.title: Repair Fable token counting and summary budgeting
changes: Fable's automatic thinking configuration now includes the required adaptive type when preserving thinking blocks. This repairs a reproduced token-count request rejection without increasing output limits or weakening counted-retry checks.

Conversation summaries now receive the configured whole-summary length target. Summary packing recognizes padded provider counts and reserves the effective output allowance, avoiding unnecessary splitting and requests without enough headroom. The length target remains guidance, not a guarantee.

These provider and context-module repairs take effect through normal component updates and a newly selected runtime generation. Existing workers and explicit source pins remain unchanged; an application update alone does not prove adoption or retry a blocked chat.

Compatible completed summary checkpoints remain usable. Unfinished summaries may need recomputation when their prompt policy changes. No original conversation is replayed or declared recovered by this release.

releases.title: Review agent permissions in the browser and across chats
changes: External agents can show their current permission requests in Unified, including the exact choices offered by the connected agent. Reloading or stopping a chat does not replay a decision.

Supporting Constellation Instances can remember matching configuration approvals across their chats. Instance owns remembered rules and its explicit Automatic setting; existing approval modes stay unchanged.
The packaged web client includes the current attachment-preview and approval controls.

releases.title: Deliver agent approvals and clarify connection failures
changes: Configuration and tool approvals now reach attached ACP clients instead of leaving a conversation waiting without a visible request. Current decisions still respect Stop, expiry and the exact saved request; no automatic or remembered approval is enabled.
Unified connection failures that are unrelated to authentication now retain their own error code and reason instead of incorrectly asking clients to sign in again.

Application builds select the public web-client source and standalone status artifact through their normal component records. The bundled client behavior is unchanged; duplicated authored web source is removed.

releases.title: Clearer update status and more reliable startup
changes: Updates now distinguishes a successfully installed application from an older component issue. Historical component warnings include their date and attempt details, and support reports include the selected failure even when it is outside the recent event list. A missing older component activation receipt alone does not request reinstallation.

Server startup reserves every configured listening address before constructing the application, avoiding app startup and diagnostic-capture side effects when a bind fails. Address and name-resolution errors give specific guidance. Existing service retry policies and authenticated readiness checks are unchanged.

Delegated agents now report fatal configured-module initialization failures before executing instead of appearing to start successfully. The existing provider-isolation exception and selected-provider checks remain in place.

Maintenance adds regression coverage for completion display identities, prepares the existing standalone status emitter for component delivery without changing its runtime behavior, and simplifies the native test workflow.

releases.title: Avoid unnecessary saves when switching chats
changes: Selecting an existing chat now keeps the lightweight selection path when unrelated workspaces are hidden, avoiding an unnecessary conversation save. When selection actually restores a folder or needs a workspace registration, it still uses the durable shared path and the same exact registration resolver.

In a synthetic 4,330-message dispatch comparison, this removed one conversation-serialization call per selection. This is not a live UI benchmark; client-private selection, pending work and folder restoration behavior remain preserved.

releases.title: Reduce repeated preparation during web updates
changes: Direct shell-resource reads and web-only state publication now reuse the existing synchronous directory-read frame, avoiding repeated preparation while assembling updates for multiple web clients. Mixed and full readers keep their existing behavior.

Durable saving still happens before publication. Each client's selections and drafts remain private, and existing invalidation rules remain unchanged. In synthetic three-client publication tests, median time fell from 197 to 170 ms and from 605 to 544 ms at two scales; these measurements are not the full live chat-loading delay.

releases.title: Retire obsolete agent waits without cancelling peer work
changes: Agents can explicitly withdraw an existing result wait with coordination.unsubscribe without cancelling the peer's work. Withdrawn waits stay withdrawn across retries and restarts; queued returns are suppressed, while already submitted or uncertain returns may still arrive. Other outstanding waits remain visible.

Authorized agents can retain reports of previously admitted work and review exact result notifications after an old task has changed, without reopening that task. Current identity, Stop, response-revision and evidence checks still apply.

This does not automatically unblock chats, resume tasks, clear a human Stop or resolve uncertain past effects. An agent must separately decide whether to resume its own dependency-blocked plan. Historical results remain available, and uncertain operations must not be replayed.

releases.title: Keep appearance validation with its canonical owner
changes: Appearance package compilation and theme validation now use the canonical appearance module without importing the application service. The existing service.validate_theme public alias remains available.
CSS validation rules, error messages, package limits, stored appearance data and permissions are unchanged. This is an internal ownership correction, with no migration or setup action required.

releases.title: Wait for an AI connection before component updates
changes: For Amplifier's own profiles, component updates now wait until the first AI connection is set up instead of starting a candidate that cannot qualify. Settings explains the wait without recording a new failed attempt. Application updates are not held by this connection check; custom profiles and overrides still use normal qualification.

After the first connection, the update owner checks the changed selection again before preparing components. Automatic updates can then continue; with automatic installation off, use Update Amplifier. Existing failures are not reclassified as harmless waiting: an earlier failed attempt remains visible until a later completed update supplies the existing recovery evidence.

Assemble Recall from the original published 0.1.0 artifact through the established component-selection mechanism. Its runtime files, public imports, stored data formats and memory behavior are unchanged. Unified remains the sole installed owner, with no standalone coinstallation or data migration.

releases.title: Lighter native activity lookup and protected release guidance
changes: Avoid repeatedly JSON-encoding validated built-in node and turn IDs when looking up native activity. Canonical validation, indexed lookup, composite and custom identity behavior remain unchanged; no new cache or storage format is introduced.

Six paired synthetic comparisons reduced activity-application time from 2.44–5.34 seconds to 0.33–0.75 seconds while preserving full, durable and late-alias results. These are bounded mechanism measurements, not a measured whole-chat or live startup speedup.

Keep every high-impact release notice and its exact wording, identity, title aliases and review acknowledgements, alongside up to the latest 256 ordinary changelog entries. Preparation and cached-history merging share the same unchanged count and UTF-8 limits, discard oldest ordinary entries first, and fail clearly if protected guidance cannot fit. Installed wording takes precedence over stale cached entries; full older ordinary history remains in Git and immutable GitHub releases. Conversation history and acknowledgement records are not deleted.

releases.title: Keep pending update cancellations attached to their work
changes: Keep an update waiter and its checkpoint receipt intact while cancellation of its exact native request is awaiting acknowledgement, including waiters already marked ready or previously suppressed. Replacement waits for that acknowledgement; changed owners, replaced rows and missing or malformed replies remain guarded.

This fixes the reproduced pending-cancellation response defect. The original live update failure did not retain its exact cancellation response, so this release does not establish that defect as its cause.

Prepare Recall storage for independent packaging while keeping its runtime files unchanged and assembled into the normal Unified installation. Public imports, stored data formats, authorization and memory behavior are unchanged; no separate component is published and no performance improvement is claimed.

releases.title: Bounded parallel verification and lighter operation updates
changes: Read at most two independent runtime source roots in parallel during each fresh verification call, preserving both existing verification boundaries, exact source checks and failure ordering. All started reads settle before the call returns; no cross-call cache or new asynchronous Stop guarantee is introduced.

In a generated, setup-warmed 45-root comparison, median paired verification time fell from 1,808.8 to 1,111.8 ms while combined parent and Git CPU use rose 14.2%. This is a bounded wall-time/CPU tradeoff, not less total work or a measured Mac or live-startup improvement.

Avoid loading retained messages and execution history when operation updates only need to validate their already-authenticated owner. Journal behavior, missing or deleting owner checks, producer permissions and recovery remain unchanged. This removes unnecessary hydration without claiming a measured live latency improvement.

releases.title: Lighter worker previews while chat work loads
changes: While the deferred Work view explicitly reports that it is still loading, omit terminal-only worker report previews before copying or hashing them. Keep current activity, unknown and mixed worker groups, worker counts and recent summaries; full report details and canonical receipts remain available.

Preserve complete compact worker views for true legacy fallbacks and for ready-empty, retrying or unavailable Work views. Qualification demonstrates reduced structural work and a smaller synthetic loading payload, not a measured live latency percentage.

releases.title: Lighter provider recovery reads and clearer update health
changes: Keep provider and model catalog recovery for a removed connection on the existing metadata-only session lookup, avoiding promotion of retained execution history into the active owner. Recovery checks, locking and saved reports are preserved. Complete detached snapshots elsewhere remain; no measured live loading-speed improvement is claimed.

On a Windows installation that has never selected a component generation, a complete update check with nothing newer can now report up to date when setup's recorded dependencies still verify. Missing or changed records, incomplete checks and recorded failures keep their existing handling. This verifies setup's record, not full component qualification, and never authorizes preparation or substitutes for a selected generation's proof.

Compare installed packages against the exact dependency record already validated, so a record disappearing during verification cannot silently skip the comparison. Update diagnostics now identify whether health is based on a generation, a setup record or neither.

releases.title: Lighter context for chat navigation
changes: Avoid copying unused workspace resource and setup details into the bundled navigation context used while loading and switching chats. Full and custom shell reads, workspace Details, setup information and resource-management actions retain their complete data.

Controlled synthetic WebSocket frames fell from 630,070 to 24,154 bytes with empty navigation demand and from 638,588 to 32,672 bytes with visible demand. These are bounded payload measurements, not a claim that live chat switching is faster by the same percentage or that all remaining loading delays are fixed.

releases.title: Windows browser sign-in codes and less repeated navigation work
changes: Avoid repeated preparation of active chat rows during one navigation query's completion check, using the existing synchronous directory read frame. Current values, nested changes, native checks and rollback are preserved, with no new cache or reuse across requests. This reduces demonstrated work; it does not establish that remaining live loading latency is eliminated.

Windows hosts with explicitly configured remote access can issue a short-lived, one-use browser sign-in code using amplifier-unified browsers code. Remote access stays off by default. Linux, macOS and WSL retain password sign-in. The deployment guide includes numbered remote-access steps; real second-device and phone-browser acceptance remains separate.

Harden browser sign-out across observed sign-out-record changes, fail closed on unreadable records, and distinguish confirmed completion from uncertain results. The documented missed-record and backward-clock limitations remain.

Recognize an installation's Windows sign-in task after a computer rename while retaining the other ownership checks. Give the update stage's own temporary session workspace a short project name to fit Windows' default path limit; user-chosen workspace names are unchanged.

During first-start self-update, the browser-open command waits for the matching host version, issues one grant request, and confirms browser opening. New Windows launchers handle arguments containing spaces and report an unconfirmed opening without automatically retrying. Existing launcher limitations remain below.

Add native regression coverage for starting again after uninstall and a separate, manually nominated candidate-runtime CI harness. The harness does not change production runtime policy or establish native qualification of the unpublished candidate.

notices.title: Use the printed address for Windows sign-in codes
notices.detail: Codes last 120 seconds and are bound to one configured HTTPS origin. A look-alike page can misuse a code disclosed during that window. Tickets or codes made or used immediately after signing out all browsers may be refused briefly; there is no per-device sign-out. An unobserved sign-out-record change can leave earlier sessions valid until expiry, another observed change or host restart.
notices.action: Enable remote access deliberately and enter the code only at the exact address printed by the local command. After sign-out, wait a few seconds before opening Amplifier or issuing another code. Follow the command's actual outcome; do not treat an uncertain sign-out as complete.

notices.title: Existing Windows launchers are not replaced by an app update
notices.detail: The computer-rename ownership repair and correct hand-over of paths containing spaces need the updated launcher. An in-app update or second setup run does not replace an older launcher. Older launchers also keep their shorter browser-open timeout and messages, although the new app's open command can continue waiting. Renamed accounts and domain/Entra/offline cases remain outside the verified scope.
notices.action: Use the supported launcher-refresh path when an existing installation needs these launcher changes; preserve the installation and follow its specific recovery guidance. During startup, look for an Amplifier browser tab before starting it again. New setup files include the current launcher; whole clean-PC update and real-browser acceptance are not claimed by runner checks.

releases.title: Less repeated work when resuming chats
changes: Native chat resume can prepare Foundation's incremental history index during the mandatory history load, avoiding a second decode on the first save. Both explicit native resume paths use this optimization; older retained Foundation workers safely keep their existing behavior.

In one finite 402 MB synthetic Foundation load-plus-first-save comparison, elapsed time fell from 2290 to 1913 milliseconds (16.5%). This is not a measurement of live whole-chat loading or a universal startup improvement.

Update checks now verify package-registry connections against current system certificates plus bundled certificate roots, addressing certificate-store gaps on new Windows installations. Failed checks retain verification and report a specific reason and next step; they do not offer an unverified update.

Windows maintenance checks and guidance now reflect Foundation's accepted folder-sharing repair: ordinary changes to entries above its ownership folders can proceed while a new worker holds ownership. Pinned folders themselves and arrivals into ownership folders remain protected. Running older workers keep their prior behavior; this development-lock alignment alone does not update installed workers.

notices.title: Package-registry checks also trust bundled certificate roots
notices.detail: Only the package-registry update lookup adds bundled roots to system trust. A root present in the bundle can be accepted even if an administrator removed it from the system store or Windows distrusts it. Certificate and hostname verification remain enabled, with no unverified fallback.
notices.action: If your organization relies on removing or distrusting a system certificate root, review this combined trust policy before updating. Bundled roots change with application dependency updates; this release does not claim complete new-PC installation or live recovery qualification.

releases.title: Reduce redundant history work during input and startup
changes: Avoid redundant history identity hashing and a second full-history copy in the internal startup callback. The original Send snapshot, complete fork history, direct preparation, authority checks and Stop behavior remain intact.
Add narrower history merge, activity, publication and native-refresh timing diagnostics without recording conversation payloads. Enclosing and inner timings overlap and must not be added together.

In scoped synthetic measurements, the second startup copy decreased from about 181 ms to 0.009 ms and host dispatch from 604 ms to 442 ms. These measurements do not establish that all live multi-second loading or switching delays are fixed.

Improve Windows setup after uninstall: restore missing app entries when safe, reuse an already-prepared runtime, show the second-run steps, and give failure guidance that does not point to a nonexistent Start-menu shortcut.

notices.title: Windows setup repair has an installed-launcher boundary
notices.detail: The setup-after-uninstall fixes include launcher code installed by setup. Rerunning a newer setup file starts the existing launcher rather than replacing it, so an installation made by an earlier setup does not automatically gain the new launcher behavior. An unprepared runtime still uses the existing preparation path.
notices.action: Do not rely on an in-app update or a second setup run to replace an older launcher. Follow the setup and launcher's reported recovery guidance; this release does not promise a verified clean-room recovery for every existing installation.

releases.title: Reduce repeated history reads during chat refresh
changes: Reuse verified execution data within native-history refresh instead of repeatedly reading and copying completed history. Public snapshots remain detached, current mutable work stays isolated, and genuine native additions retain the full fallback.

In one synthetic successor measurement against the retained identical-input baseline, first refresh decreased from 2,492 to 2,166 ms and CPU time from 1,528 to 1,144 ms (13.1% and 25.1%). This is not statistical, live or universal startup proof; initial index publication still costs about 1.57 seconds.

Use the workspace-location boundary for manual selection and conversation navigation while preserving existing workspace IDs, exact registered paths, unavailable locations, pins, Canvas and saved-chat restart behavior.

Give new Windows installations a shorter source-store folder name so default modules fit the accepted installation-path budget with long paths disabled. Existing installations keep their original store and are not moved or renamed.
Keep established product websites primary in the ecosystem documentation.

notices.title: Windows path-budget fix applies to new installations
notices.detail: New Windows setup uses the source folder name s, allowing the measured default modules to fit an installation root of up to 59 characters. Existing installations retain source-store and its previous 54-character root limit; an in-app update or a second setup run does not migrate that folder.
notices.action: Keep an existing source store in place; do not manually rename it to apply this fix. When choosing a new installation location, stay within the setup path limit.

releases.title: Keep recurring chat updates focused on current work
changes: Avoid promoting completed execution history into the current owner when reading metadata for runtime placement, Stop, task controls and model catalogs. Worker requests still receive full detached snapshots.
Keep the small current execution owner during empty or fully web-shadowed native refreshes. Real native additions retain the complete-history fallback rather than silently omitting work.

In one controlled pair with 24,560 nodes and 12,598 receipts, a later event plus flush improved from 248 to 35 ms and CPU time from 232 to 5 ms. The first saved-v1 changed-revision refresh was slower (642 to 2,976 ms), and the first event was 269 versus 277 ms. This improves recurring updates, not initial loading; it is not a live performance claim.

Select the published workspace-metadata 0.2.0 component, adding an immutable local-location view while keeping workspace registration as the sole writable owner. Existing workspace IDs, history, settings and host behavior are unchanged.

releases.title: Faster switching and updates in long-running chats
changes: Keep completed execution history out of ordinary current-work updates, reducing repeated history loading while preserving full history, late corrections, earlier paging and restart readback.

In the qualified synthetic large-chat comparison using the real app service and built client, median chat switching improved from 322 to 227 ms, worst switching from 966 to 309 ms, and Stop from 633 to 283 ms. First admission of the old chat was slower during conversion (2.26 to 4.47 seconds); these measurements are not a blanket cold-start or live-workload speedup claim.
Clarify installation guidance and the relationships between Amplifier ecosystem components.

notices.title: Preserve state when rolling back
notices.detail: This release can save execution history in a typed storage format that older application versions refuse to read or collect. Downgrading the application binary alone does not make that state compatible.
notices.action: Preserve it and reopen with a compatible version, or deliberately restore a complete earlier backup with its known recovery point. Do not rewrite storage pointers to bypass the format check.

releases.title: More output room for conversation summaries
changes: Raise the implicit portable-summary generation allowance from 8,192 to 32,768 tokens for qualifying advertised large-context, high-output profiles. Explicit user limits remain unchanged; smaller or unknown profiles retain a conservative allowance and providers still enforce their actual limits.

Bind partial summary checkpoints to the resolved model, output allowance and reasoning effort. Reject incomplete summaries and stale asynchronous configuration, while preserving original conversation history and completed tool receipts.

Stop on unclassified provider limit errors rather than repeatedly splitting and resubmitting summary source. Only a locally established input-fit refusal permits source splitting; no automatic output-budget escalation is added.

notices.title: Summary allowance and component adoption
notices.detail: Qualifying profiles may generate longer summaries, with additional time and token cost. Existing explicit limits are preserved. Legacy or changed partial checkpoints may need regeneration from the originals, including already-paid fragments. This does not establish that every blocked conversation will recover or resolve independent token-counting failures.
notices.action: Use the normal component update path, including Other components when offered, and a supported worker replacement to load the repaired context-managed component.
