Confirm the effective summary allowance before continuing a blocked conversation. An app update alone is not proof of component adoption; preserve Stop and reconcile pending operations before one guarded continuation.

releases.title: Clearer controls, expanded details and Settings focus
changes: Improve padding and wrapping for Copy and Save diagnostics, align error-detail actions, and make expanded Work, question, Canvas and workspace details easier to distinguish from their parent rows.

Restore visible keyboard focus when handling unsaved Settings edits, including short windows and retained scroll positions. Remove the persistent visible Return hint and its empty space while keeping accessible help, the Writing preference and the existing Return behavior.

Maintain the peer-caption and manager-placement test fixtures without changing production attribution, cancellation or recovery policy. This release refines existing presentation and focus behavior; it does not claim every Settings state, physical keyboard or live recovery path has been requalified.

releases.title: Clearer checkout moves and safe recovery checks
changes: The task execution-folder card now shows plain move states, the actual source and target folders, and continuation status separately. Use Check move to refresh the same receipt without entering internal IDs or writing a verification explanation.

Checkout moves avoid a duplicate history checkpoint and use the existing authoritative save and release boundary. The host recognizes the actual native writer rather than its launcher, retains the original boundary reply through delayed confirmation, and reports Needs recovery when cleanup cannot yet be proved instead of waiting indefinitely.

notices.title: Proven task moves can finish after restart
notices.detail: On startup, Unified can finish an existing move or record that it did not move only when retained receipts and current ownership prove the outcome. An already-active task can receive its guarded continuation after confirmed placement. A missing reply alone is never proof of success.
notices.action: Use Check move to refresh the existing record. It does not start a move, release a writer or replay inputs. Stop and genuinely uncertain release or placement remain blocking; use the original owner's supported recovery when Needs recovery remains.

releases.title: Avoid an unnecessary history copy during context preservation
changes: Context preservation now checkpoints through the existing synchronous history visitor without creating a detached history copy that would be discarded.

Keep every save, writer guard, anchor, recovery, failure and cancellation behavior unchanged, including detached results for callers that request them and the existing getter fallback. This removes temporary work in one path; it is not a promise of faster whole turns or model responses.

releases.title: Observe context preparation in opt-in timing diagnostics
changes: Opt-in context-view timing now observes the registered asynchronous context callbacks actually used by the worker, using the existing diagnostic phases and transport. Diagnostics remain off by default; this improves coverage, not execution speed.

Keep the method fallback when no observable callback is registered, and avoid duplicate spans when a callback delegates to that method. Custom contexts that mix registered callbacks with direct legacy calls can still have unobserved legacy requests; missing marks alone do not prove no work occurred.

releases.title: Reduce temporary encoding during context preservation
changes: Preserve conversation context with less temporary encoding: hash the same canonical message array one row at a time, and avoid a redundant size encoding for tool messages that are already clearly large.

Keep checkpoint ordering, fresh content hashes after checkpoint waits, recovery, failed-save handling and cancellation unchanged. This refines the context-preservation path; it does not change saved history, model context limits or provider behavior, and is not a promise of faster whole turns or model responses.

releases.title: Select the published publishing component
changes: Unified now assembles its existing publishing support from the exact published component artifact, retaining its source provenance and license in the application package.
Publishing runtime code, dependencies and policies are unchanged; components/publishing remains the authoring source and the generated selected delivery is the assembly input.

releases.title: Verified cleanup code and leaner status polling
changes: Before local Docker cleanup can preserve files or enter the backend, verify that the same waiting helper loaded the worker and retention code from captured source bytes matching the running application's qualified release wheel. Recheck permissions, Stop, ownership, revision and original operation evidence before permitting that helper to continue.

Retain a small, content-free loaded-input receipt with the original cleanup operation. Reading that receipt does not start a helper or contact the backend, and does not claim that an old process is still running, that cleanup was dispatched, or that an earlier uncertain operation is resolved.

Keep Incus and registered remote-runner cleanup on their existing routes without claiming this local Docker attestation. The proof covers the named application inputs, not the interpreter or its complete dependency closure.

Reduce repeated work in native status polling by sharing the existing request-scoped directory read frame. Each poll still observes current facts with its existing paging and signed-cursor protections; this adds no cross-request cache and starts no agent work. This improves the status-reading path, not model response time or all chat loading.

notices.title: Local Docker cleanup requires a qualified application installation
notices.detail: Local Docker removal and finish-cleanup now refuse to start when the running application's original qualified release-wheel evidence is unavailable or its helper inputs do not match. Source/development or otherwise unqualified installations can therefore no longer use this cleanup path. An update or this new evidence does not resolve an earlier UNKNOWN operation, clear Stop, or authorize cleanup of a stopped environment.
notices.action: Use the normal supported update or installation path to obtain a qualified application. Inspect the original cleanup receipt and current ownership before any separately authorized new cleanup; do not retry an uncertain operation or bypass a refusal.

releases.title: Use the selected outputs component in application packages
changes: Build and install the existing outputs helpers from the selected, published component artifact through Unified's normal offline assembly workflow. The selected runtime bytes match the helpers already shipped, and Unified remains their only installed owner.

Include the selected component's provenance and license in the application package. Editing or publishing the separate outputs authoring project no longer silently changes the application's normal or editable builds; runtime behavior, dependencies, saved history and execution permissions are unchanged.

releases.title: Clearer save diagnostics and verified headless connections
changes: Add small, content-free measurements to the existing bounded slow-operation log: whether a save used the full or an explicit admitted scope, and whether its message, execution and worker containers were already resident, cold or unavailable.

Collect these measurements without loading conversation bodies or changing saved history, cancellation, permissions or execution. This is diagnostic follow-through for investigating loading and queue delays, not a claim that those delays are fixed.

Headless commands connecting to an existing host now use normal verified system or environment trust for user-supplied certificates, while retaining the local CA for Unified's app-owned certificate pair. If certificate verification fails for every suitable configured origin, report that failure instead of starting an unintended local fallback.

releases.title: Open long chats with less waiting
changes: Opening a chat now displays the 20 most recent messages first instead of 100, reducing the initial rendering work for long, richly formatted conversations. Earlier messages remain available through the existing history controls in pages of up to 100.
Keep the full saved conversation and model context unchanged. Message identities, attachments, editing, drafts, execution permissions and Stop behavior retain their existing meaning.

notices.title: Long chats initially show the latest 20 messages
notices.detail: A chat opens with a smaller recent-message view to reduce loading delay. This changes only the initial web display; no saved messages are deleted and the conversation supplied to the model is not shortened by this setting.
notices.action: Use the existing earlier-history controls when you want to read older messages. Explicit history pages still contain up to 100 messages.

releases.title: Preserve selected test artifacts during cleanup recovery
changes: Fix an already-qualified cleanup recovery path that could stop at an absolute virtual-environment interpreter link when only test artifacts were selected for retention. It now preserves the complete bounded archive, including inert link and FIFO metadata, without extracting it or opening those targets.

Record archive-only custody explicitly and preserve it during passive removal inspection. Ordinary artifact exports remain strict; original-source verification, fresh archive creation, stopped-owner and backend checks, dispatch receipts and physical-absence checks still govern cleanup.

releases.title: Clearer chat layout and safer Return-key editing
changes: Conversation error banners now follow the same reading width as the chat and message box. Long explanations and recovery/reporting actions wrap on narrow screens without covering the dismiss control.
Checkbox labels, selectors, compound-field focus, Settings groups and loading/error/retry rows have more consistent spacing. Narrow upload and document-action controls wrap within their panel.

Return inserts a new line by default on mobile, tablet and touch-capable browsers. Clearly desktop-only browsers retain Enter-to-send. An Always insert a new line preference is saved in this browser; the visible guidance explains the effective behavior, and explicit Send remains available.

Rich-text Return handling avoids duplicate edits and preserves list/code/table continuation, undo, composition guards and drafts. Compact message-box controls stay aligned, with Return guidance outside the writing border.

notices.title: Return adds a new line on touch-capable browsers
notices.detail: Automatic Return behavior now favors editing on mobile, tablet and touch-capable devices, including touch-capable computers: Return inserts a new line rather than sending. Clearly desktop-only devices still use Enter to send. The Return preference applies only in this browser and does not change another browser's setting.
notices.action: Use the Send button to submit a message on a touch-capable device. Check the guidance beside the message box; choose Always insert a new line if you want that behavior on a desktop too.

releases.title: Reduce repeated work when saving execution progress
changes: Saving ongoing work reuses hashes already computed during that save, reducing repeated processing while preserving the full saved record and recovery checks.
Computation uses the verified published kernels package through the existing bundled delivery path; installed behavior and permissions remain unchanged.

releases.title: Keep busy conversations responsive as coordination history grows
changes: Recent coordination updates now read only the newest matching requests, reducing repeated work while managers and workers exchange messages. Saved request order, cancellation status and history remain unchanged.

releases.title: Keep busy workspaces responsive
changes: Browser updates share one notice-counting pass, reducing repeated database work while chats and tools are active. Unread counts, approvals, errors and saved conversations retain their existing behavior.

releases.title: Keep context-limit recovery connected to the original request
changes: Preserve a model provider's context-limit feedback when the host adds the selected model and current observations to a request, so the existing recovery path can use the feedback instead of losing it between request wrappers.

Keep recovery tied to the exact failed request and its options. Changed requests, feedback already consumed, and errors after streamed output do not start another recovery attempt; Stop and completed-tool receipts remain intact.

Add regression coverage for cold Fable 5.2 counting, recovery during a long tool turn, resumed signed history, a second context-limit refusal and Stop. The upstream cold-model fix is selected in development checks; installed provider components still update through the normal component-update path.
Package workspace registration metadata from its published 0.1.0 component, including its source and license records. The runtime code and workspace behavior are unchanged.

releases.title: Published operations component, unchanged runtime behavior
changes: Unified now selects the original published operations 0.1.0 artifact and verifies its runtime bytes offline. Independent component authoring moves to components/operations, while the selected top-level runtime keeps the existing editable and isolated-worker imports. Unified remains the only installed distribution owner; operation behavior, durable receipts, cursors, authority and Stop controls are unchanged. The app package adds the selected artifact's provenance and license records; it does not republish the component.

Component release tooling now supports the independent workspace-metadata publication path, without changing Unified's selected runtime or coinstalling a standalone package. MCP guidance documents the released error-fidelity adapter in its explicit opt-in profile.

releases.title: Clearer model costs, browser sign-out and Windows recovery
changes: Model pricing and usage views use provider-supplied fixed or tiered prices, including cache modifiers and whole-request tiers when supplied. Missing and partial costs keep their explanations through streaming, saved accounting and work totals; known zero remains zero and historical usage is not repriced.

The owner command amplifier-unified browsers sign-out ends earlier browser sessions, pending sign-in tickets and open state streams. No browser is signed out merely by installing this release. This signs out all browsers, not one selected device; terminals and other clients retain their own access credentials.

Windows owners gain a separate launcher-refresh command that verifies the exact installation, retains rollback evidence and waits for files still held by closing workers. An ordinary in-app application update does not replace the stable launcher. A failed or interrupted refresh keeps an explicit recovery outcome rather than reporting unverified success.

Windows status retains a bounded private failure reason and checks the active application generation instead of treating an older launcher as the running version. The launcher distinguishes an unreachable or restarting host from a rejected TLS identity and waits briefly for a restart before asking the person to open the app again.

New app-owned chat folders on Windows use a shorter recorded project name; existing chat history stays in its recorded folder and user-chosen folders are unchanged. The accepted Foundation source-store fix handles long paths and gives new Windows entries shorter names without moving existing entries. A setup limitation remains: the deepest default module imports need an installation-folder path of at most 54 characters, although setup accepts 59. A newer worker's short entry can appear unverified to an older host until that host is updated; the entry remains intact. Other platforms keep their existing paths.

Windows uninstall stops the app and removes its sign-in task before removing shortcuts and Apps-list entries. A failed earlier step keeps those entries and does not touch the certificate; uninstall can be repeated and asks before interrupting active chat work. At the end, Windows asks once whether to delete this installation's own trusted certificate, with No selected by default. Declining or a blocked removal still finishes uninstall and explains that the certificate remains. Program files and saved data remain. These launcher changes require a new setup file or the separate launcher-refresh command, not an in-app update alone.

Application releases publish the same verified Windows setup bytes under a stable version-less download name as well as the versioned name. It is an alias of that release's installer, not another build; component publications do not replace the latest application release.

First-install runtime preparation now snapshots the existing shared settings, credentials and routing together into its private candidate before the existing configured validation, matching the updater's established preparation path. It does not change the live shared configuration or send model input merely to prepare the runtime.

Unified now selects the original published worktrees and portability 0.1.0 artifacts through its offline component assembly. Portability verifies its exact selected worktrees receipt. Unified remains the single installed distribution owner; the existing component runtime bytes are unchanged and the package adds their provenance and license records.

Deployment guidance explains the explicitly configured MCP profile for supported Work ACP retrieval and maps Unified's external roles to the existing Constellation public boundaries. Installation-repair controls present in the selected client remain unavailable until the separate host repair feature is accepted and released; this release does not enable or qualify that pending repair workflow.

releases.title: Release idle external-agent workers and keep saved chats ready to resume
changes: External agents that support Unified's optional cleanup handshake can release a settled worker when the existing idle, capacity or component-update policy requests it. Ordinary turn completion keeps the worker warm; active work and pending decisions continue to prevent cleanup.

The next message resumes the same saved external-agent chat. Unconfirmed cleanup retains the connection and is reconciled before sending new work; previous messages are not replayed. In a group chat, other participants can continue while one participant cleans up.

Dismiss or restore an old held or uncertain steering warning without resending the instruction. Current active and queued instructions stay visible, and a later confirmed delivery updates the warning.
The portability component is available as a separate verified package with its exact published worktrees dependency. Unified continues to include both components in its normal installation.

releases.title: Windows setup uses one short folder, and helper programs stay windowless
changes: Windows setup now installs into one short folder (Amplifier, in your local app data folder), and a second run of setup offers to open the installation that is already there.
Windows setup now says in plain words why it stopped and what to do next, and it tries an interrupted download again.

On Windows, programs that the app starts now share one hidden console and no longer open terminal windows, unless a program asks Windows for a window of its own; existing installations get this with the in-app update.
A password question that such a program asks in its console is not visible, so use a credential helper or an SSH agent for Git.

On a Windows installation from setup 0.94.0 or later, setup-tls force now creates a new local certificate after you add a LAN or Tailnet address, and Windows asks you to confirm it once; sign-in from another device is not available on Windows yet.

releases.title: Windows setup without a manual certificate import
changes: On a new Windows installation, you no longer import a certificate by hand. The first time the app opens, Amplifier shows one short message. Then Windows asks one question about a certificate named "Amplifier Unified (this PC only)". Select Yes.
If you select No, the app keeps running and nothing on the PC changes. Open Amplifier again to get the question again.
The certificate works only for the private connection between your browser and Amplifier on this PC. Its signing key is never saved, so it cannot be used to make a certificate for a website.

If the security settings of the PC do not allow this step, the app says so and saves the certificate in the export folder of the installation, so that IT support can trust it. Amplifier changes no security setting.

Existing Windows installations are unchanged. They keep their current certificate, and Amplifier never adds that certificate to Windows by itself. The new step comes only with a setup file from this release or later, because an in-app update does not replace the launcher that setup installed.

Limits on a new Windows installation: adding a LAN or Tailnet address is not available yet. The certificate is valid for 825 days, and its renewal is not automated yet. Removing the app does not remove the certificate from Windows yet. This work is in progress.
With the new setup file, messages from the Windows launcher open in front of other windows.

New optional sign-in for an isolated installation on a Unix host: the owner can sign in with the normal host account through a private local sign-in bridge (setting host_pam). It is off by default, and the default sign-in does not change. If the bridge is missing or refuses, sign-in is denied. There is no fallback to another password, and the app does not save the password. See "Sign in with the installing host owner's account" in the deployment guide. Windows does not accept this setting.
Maintenance: the separate worktrees component can now be published as its own package under its own tag. The app, its dependencies and its release channel do not change.

The new certificate and the Windows trust step are tested on a hosted Windows machine, including a check with Edge. The complete setup with the real Windows question on a clean Windows 11 PC is still being tested. The optional host sign-in was tested on Linux.

releases.title: Windows setup chooses and saves a free local address
changes: Windows setup now chooses a free local address (port) by itself and saves it. It no longer uses the fixed port 8942. Before, setup stopped when another program, another Windows account on the same PC, or a Windows feature already held that port.
The app keeps the saved address at every start and after every update. Shortcuts read it, so you never type a port.

If another program later uses the saved address, or Windows reserves it, the app says which of the two happened. It then offers to move to a new local address, and moves only when you select Yes. Your chats, settings and accounts stay. An app window that you installed from the browser must be installed again, and messages that you typed but did not send are not carried over.
The app never takes over or stops another program that uses the address.

Existing Windows installations keep their current address, including 8942, and start as before. The new message and the offer to move arrive only with a setup file from this release or later, because an in-app update does not replace the launcher that setup installed.
The config set command accepts several settings in one call (config set KEY VALUE KEY VALUE) and saves them in one write.
On Linux, macOS and WSL the local address does not change.

Address selection is tested on a hosted Windows machine against a real listening program and a real Windows reservation. The message window has not yet been seen on a real Windows desktop. The complete setup on a clean Windows 11 PC, and two Windows accounts on one PC, are still being tested.

releases.title: Windows setup installs a working shell for the assistant
changes: Windows setup now installs the complete Git for Windows 2.56.0 in place of the smaller MinGit. This gives the assistant a bash shell and the common command-line tools on a PC that has no developer tools.
The assistant uses this private bash first, also on a PC that has WSL. To use WSL for shell commands, set AMPLIFIER_BASH_WINDOWS_SHELL=wsl.
Setup starts the private shell and checks that it runs its own Git before it reports a finished installation.
During setup, the Git download is now about 119 MB (before: about 40 MB). Git uses about 425 MB on disk.
Existing Windows installations keep their current Git, because an in-app update does not replace the tools that setup installed. This release adds no way to refresh them.
On Windows, the app no longer takes a program from the current project folder when it looks up a command by name. A file named bash, git or uv in a project cannot take the place of the real tool.
The new shell is checked on a hosted Windows machine. The complete setup on a clean Windows 11 PC is still being tested.

releases.title: Simpler managed testing with Docker Compose
changes: Use the installed DTU Smart Tool and its ordinary package-update lineage for local Docker testing, without per-operation whole-environment attestation or target-local certification. Setup observes the existing daemon, Compose and base image; it does not install a daemon or adopt another owner's environment. Explicit Incus and connected-machine qualification remain separate.

Choose a trusted Compose file from copied source, or use the maintained Python, browser and new app-preview presets. Default Python and browser presets still prepare their locked dependencies automatically; an explicit custom Compose file takes over that preparation. Preview ports are loopback-only, and copied-source checks do not implicitly grant host credentials, Docker sockets, writable original-source mounts or privileged host namespaces.

New disposable Docker test environments allow ordinary networking by default, including dependency and build commands. Select offline: true when a check must run without external networking. Incus keeps its existing offline execution boundary.

New disposable Docker copies retain the original source snapshot, results, receipts and selected /artifacts output without requiring a full guest-workspace export. Select preserveSource: true before starting when changes made anywhere in the guest workspace must also be exported. Existing environment owners retain their original preservation contract; old archives and failed or uncertain receipts are not deleted or reclassified.

Keep resource ownership, operator limits, Stop and exact backend identities in force across normal runner updates. Known failures before a helper starts are distinguished from admitted or uncertain backend work. This release does not replay unknown operations, migrate existing environments or settle historical cleanup incidents.

notices.title: New Docker tests have network access by default
notices.detail: New managed Docker environments now permit ordinary networking instead of defaulting to an internal offline network. Default Python and browser dependency preparation remains available. This does not supply host credentials or change existing environment bindings; Incus keeps its separate offline boundary.
notices.action: Set offline: true explicitly when creating a Docker check or environment that must not access external networks. Review trusted custom Compose inputs and dependency commands for the intended workload.

notices.title: Full guest-workspace export is optional for new disposable Docker tests
notices.detail: The original source snapshot, results, receipts and selected /artifacts are retained. By default, changes elsewhere inside a new disposable Docker guest are not exported before removal. Existing owners keep their original full-source preservation contract, and failed selected exports still block destruction.
notices.action: Save reports, patches and build outputs to /artifacts. Set preserveSource: true before starting if you also need the complete guest workspace exported. Do not use this change as permission to replay an uncertain cleanup or remove another owner's environment.

releases.title: Keep Windows update helpers windowless
changes: On Windows, the helper programs that the app starts to check packages, update, verify and restore an installation now run without opening a console window. Their commands, time limits and stop behavior are unchanged.
On Windows, the feedback upload helper also runs without a console window.
The app's locked dependencies now select the Amplifier Foundation revision that keeps its Git and dependency helper programs windowless on Windows.
This covers the named update, verification, package and feedback helpers. It is not yet confirmed to remove every console window at Windows sign-in; that work continues.

When an update cannot read the decision-model account list, update diagnostics now record a fixed failure type and basic facts such as elapsed time, output size, exit code and system error code. They never record program output, file paths, commands or credentials. The check still fails safely and does not retry by itself.

releases.title: Keep voice message alignment independent of history services
changes: Voice message alignment now uses the shared message identity helper directly, avoiding host history dependencies in isolated workers. Existing voice message identities and repeated-utterance matching remain unchanged.

releases.title: Keep native message checkpoints lightweight
changes: Keep native response and peer checkpoints focused on message records without loading host history, workspace catalogs or configuration just to prepare displayed messages. Existing message IDs, public visibility, provenance, timestamps, voice and attachment behavior are unchanged.

Share the existing native message projection rules between checkpoints and host history. This is internal maintenance: it adds no new message mode, storage migration, setting, permission or automatic replay, and requires no user action.

releases.title: Workspace metadata maintenance
changes: Keeps workspace registration, listing and search rules together in one small metadata component. Existing workspace IDs, names, custom fields, history, selection, pins, permissions and saved data keep their current behavior.

Keeps native response saving separate from host-only workspace catalog reconciliation without expanding worker access. Unified remains the only installed owner of the bundled metadata component; this is internal packaging maintenance, not a separate package publication or a new workspace mode. No settings change or migration is required.

releases.title: Use the published scheduling package in Unified builds
changes: Build Unified with the explicitly selected scheduling 0.1.0 published artifact, keeping its exact runtime snapshot, license and provenance in the application. Scheduling development or a later component publication no longer changes the app's selected snapshot by itself. Unified remains the sole installed package owner; do not install a separate scheduling distribution over it.

Preserve the existing scheduling runtime and policy, saved schedules, run identities and uncertain-outcome handling. This packaging change introduces no new scheduler process, database migration, independent scheduling updater or automatic replay. App updates and rollback continue through the existing Unified path, and Windows retains the selected package's timezone-data requirement. No migration or setting change is required.

releases.title: Clearer delivery recovery and workspace maintenance
changes: Close an inactive failed or uncertain local delivery item without resending it or discarding its original input, text or attachment references. Find closed items in Chat info or the pre-chat screen to inspect or reopen them without sending. Closure survives reload and reconnect; a late passive check cannot reopen the item, and exact positive acceptance still retires it. Active sends cannot be closed, and existing collapsed warnings are not automatically converted.

Make passive delivery checks avoid redundant command-journal writes, full history refresh and copying unrelated execution history. A check still does not send or retry work; newly confirmed acceptance reconciles the original receipt, while dormant chats retain their existing admission and recovery checks.

Consolidate the internal rules for adding, renaming, archiving, restoring and removing workspace registrations with the existing discovery metadata owner. Existing workspace names, custom metadata and registration IDs are preserved; adding an already registered folder changes its name only when an explicit name is supplied.

Keep folder validation and creation, workspace selection, pins, Canvas effects and saved native conversation history with their existing host owners. This is internal maintenance, not a new workspace registry, identity migration or permission change. No migration or setting change is required.

releases.title: Read earlier public messages in shared agent rooms
changes: Let supported external agents in a shared room request earlier committed public messages and continue the text of long messages when needed. Reads use the existing saved-message owner, with source attribution, bounded pages and explicit omissions; private agent context, tools, interrupted partial replies and unsent drafts stay separate.

Offer room-context tools through an optional standard HTTP MCP attachment when the agent advertises that capability and Unified has a primary configured HTTPS public address. That address must be reachable and trusted from the agent's runtime; configuration alone does not establish remote connectivity or TLS trust. Missing capability or HTTPS configuration leaves ordinary chat usable.

Scope each transport credential to the current room, participant and saved source binding. Membership and source changes are checked before reading and again before returning an asynchronous result. This grants no other room, private history or host-control access. Revocation prevents future reads but cannot erase content an agent already received.

Preserve the saved agent session identity when attaching context tools on creation or resume. An advertised attachment failure remains an explicit connection failure rather than silently removing the tools, creating a replacement session or replaying work. Existing singleton and directed chats and Stop's execution behavior remain unchanged.

releases.title: Shared agent rooms and simpler conversation delivery
changes: Add several external agents to a new shared chat. Send one message to the room; agents can respond to you and one another without choosing a recipient. Agents can work concurrently while you keep posting. Participation may use model calls even when an agent chooses not to reply; Stop interrupts the room's current exchange.

Existing native chats, single-agent chats and saved directed groups keep their existing chat modes. Shared-room participation is a distinct new-room choice, not an automatic conversion of saved conversations.

Ordinary native Send addresses the conversation rather than the browser's last observed run. The native owner can guide an eligible active response, deliver at its next request boundary, or start a new turn after normal completion. Explicit run-anchored steering stays strict and does not become new work.

Keep a pending message's captured conversation source, text, attachments, quotes and settings checks through waits and navigation. Switching chats does not redirect it. Stop still fences submissions prepared before it; uncertain submissions retain their original identity, and Check delivery observes the saved receipt without resending.

Improve native worker lifecycle and health feedback so admission, completion and retained failure evidence stay distinct. This does not introduce a new delivery mode, manual queue, permission or automatic replay of uncertain work.

Clarify guidance for roots and native delegated workers, including repeated worker preparation and stored versus request-only reminders. Guidance distinguishes unavailable optional work from an essential blocker: continue independent authorized work where possible and report the concrete blocker when the assigned result depends on it. This changes guidance and role preparation, not permissions, task authority or automatic recovery, and does not guarantee a model will always follow it.

Add an independent scheduling package publisher without changing Unified's installed scheduling dependency or behavior. Component artifact publication is separate from application release publication; this does not select or co-install that separate package in existing installations.

notices.title: Ordinary Send follows the conversation, not a captured run
notices.detail: An ordinary native message may guide current work, wait for the next request boundary, or start a new turn after normal completion. Explicit run-anchored steering remains strict. Stop, captured source and configuration checks still apply. Previously uncertain saved submissions are not automatically replayed.
notices.action: No setting change is required. Use ordinary Send for a message to the conversation and Stop to interrupt current work. For an uncertain submission, use Check delivery to inspect its saved receipt rather than sending a duplicate; form a fresh retry only after definite rejection with the original target available.

releases.title: End settled worker management without losing history
changes: An assignment owner can now end management of a settled worker even when its saved task is unfinished or an earlier settings change failed. Retirement frees the member slot without marking the task successful, changing its saved task or settings, clearing Stop, deleting history or resuming work.

Active writers and settings work, pending or uncertain input and calls, checkout handoffs, shared task claims and unsettled test resources still block retirement. Retired workers with unfinished or unreadable task state cannot use standing automatic readmission; starting new work remains a separate authorized action.

Updated collaboration guidance and focused checks for stopped workers, retained failure records and separate readmission. This release does not itself retire existing chats or repair an earlier saved-versus-loaded settings mismatch.

Fixed fresh installation dependency resolution by having the shipped Foundation and session-naming defaults follow their common main source, matching Memory. New default worker preparations follow the same source; explicit installed pins, forks and existing runtime generations keep their recorded selections.

releases.title: Less handoff clutter in chats
changes: Remove Past handoffs and completed delivery cards from chats. Pending chat proposals and failed or uncertain delivery remain available where action may be needed.
Stop loading completed handoff history into chat controls while keeping saved receipts that prevent duplicate chat creation and opening messages.

releases.title: Clearer guidance for reading saved conversations
changes: Clarified the assistant's guidance for finding saved conversations and distinguishing conversation text, captured execution evidence and current task receipts. The guidance preserves scoped passive reads, private drafts and the distinction between reading a chat and continuing its work.

Added focused checks for the guidance delivered to the model and its packaged reference. This does not add transcript tools, change Context Intelligence capture or routing capabilities, or alter your selected bundles and settings.

releases.title: Useful workspace defaults and simpler starter editing
changes: Keep automatic bundle defaults separate from choices you saved explicitly. Ordinary workspaces use the general Work fallback, while the built-in Amplifier development starter uses Work AmpDev when no app, shared or workspace choice overrides it. Existing conversations keep their saved choices.

Let automatically configured Amplifier development workspaces follow later shipped starter defaults instead of keeping an accidental literal pin. On POSIX hosts, startup converts only unchanged generated settings backed by matching built-in starter, setup, placement and directory records; ambiguous or edited settings stay untouched.

Edit a built-in workspace starter immediately, then Save as new starter without duplicating it first. Custom starters offer Save changes or Save as new starter; every edited field is preserved, while built-in definitions remain unchanged. Unknown saves retain their exact recovery command rather than creating another copy.
Keep Windows application rollback bound to the still-serving installation when a launch pointer has already changed, with its original package, data-owner and TLS checks preserved.
Bring the shipped appearance-authoring and conversation-surface guidance in line with the current supported controls, with clearer everyday-user and low-effort interaction guidance.

notices.title: Automatic starter defaults can follow the shipped release
notices.detail: New automatic Amplifier development setups record starter intent rather than an explicit bundle pin. Explicit app, shared, project, local and draft choices still win, even when their value equals an older default. Blank, Development and custom starters with no bundle inherit the general fallback, not the Amplifier development specialization. Existing chats are not switched. A narrowly proven unchanged legacy Amplifier development settings file may be converted on POSIX hosts; shared/app settings, custom definitions and ambiguous files are not migrated. A manual rewrite that is byte-identical to the original generated file cannot be distinguished from that file.
notices.action: No action is needed to follow automatic defaults. To keep a specific bundle for future chats, save an explicit bundle choice in Settings or the workspace's local override. If you manually maintained a generated starter settings file, use an explicit local override before updating rather than relying on an indistinguishable same-byte rewrite. Review the chosen bundle before starting a new chat; this release does not change an existing chat's saved bundle.

releases.title: Computer sessions follow the work that owns them
changes: Keep computer-use ownership tied to the actual task: UI-use holds one episode through selection and final verification, while direct desktop calls and delegated workers keep their own exact execution lifetimes.

Fence new desktop input immediately on Stop, and retain asynchronous cleanup until input release and the indicator have both settled. Finishing a task or losing a worker process is not treated as proof that the desktop has been released.

Bound waits for unfinished cleanup without replacing the original task result or silently acquiring a new desktop owner. Passive status can reconcile retained custody; confirmed settlement can allow the same idle owner to park safely.

Update the optional native-desktop package to the accepted computer-use lifecycle implementation, including its macOS framework dependency declaration. Explicit older bundle selections and opt-outs remain respected; existing workers are not rewritten.

notices.title: Computer access now retains task-owned cleanup
notices.detail: Newly prepared workers using the current computer-use bundle retain desktop ownership through real task and native cleanup boundaries. A pending or uncertain release can keep new input, reattachment or idle parking blocked instead of assuming cleanup succeeded. Episode ownership and the persistent activity panel currently apply to supported macOS targets. Ownership is cooperative among Amplifier sessions on a controller/channel, not exclusive desktop control; Linux and Windows keep their existing disclosure and indicators.
notices.action: Respond to the normal disclosure on the controlled computer when access begins. Use the existing Stop controls to interrupt input; Resume clears only the host UI latch, not an old episode or the bundle's durable halt. If cleanup is unconfirmed, check status or stop the conversation; neither proves release. Confirm on the controlled computer rather than deleting receipts or retrying uncertain input.

releases.title: Attach ACP clients to your running Unified host
changes: Use amplifier-unified acp to connect an ACP client to an existing authenticated Unified host. Attachments share the host and support exact chat resume, streamed text and tool updates, and Stop scoped to the attached chat.

Disconnect an ACP client without cancelling work that the host already accepted. Safely reattach after an idle MCP worker has released ownership; busy, protected or uncertain owners still refuse replacement. Local connections reuse the configured listener and exact certificate pin.

Preserve verified manual-install provenance during Windows update activation and failed-candidate rollback. A repaired installation is independently checked against its own official package while preserving the original owner and data binding; unverifiable or changed proof still refuses.
Improve maintained CLI history-refresh and reconnect test fixtures without changing the application behavior they check.

releases.title: Resource safety without manual reservations
changes: Remove manual resource reservation forms, claim reads and reservation-only execution limits. Work no longer needs an arbitrary resource key or stale-claim reconciliation before it can continue.
Keep real resource inventory, managed task storage, recorded resource lifecycles and machine-capacity safeguards. Existing physical owners still control their own safety and cleanup.

Load existing execution settings without the two retired reservation quotas, preserving other positive limits and normal revision checks. Historical claim rows and receipts remain intact and inactive.

notices.title: Manual resource reservations have been retired
notices.detail: The workspace.resources.reservations, workspace.resources.reserve, workspace.resources.release and workspace.resources.uncertain actions are no longer supported. The two reservation-only execution limits are removed. Existing claim records remain as historical evidence; they do not gate work and are not marked released.
notices.action: Remove calls to these four actions from scripts and instructions. Do not reconcile or release old claims. This change does not stop or delete physical resources; continue to use their actual owners and existing cleanup checks.

releases.title: Preserve saved-child identity across credential refreshes
changes: Compare retained child setup using the same credential-field rules as saved snapshots, so refreshing credentials does not by itself look like a changed child configuration. Authorization, required credentials and real provider or noncredential configuration changes still enforce their existing checks.

Keep native-provider test preparation on the locked dependency selection instead of replacing it with an incompatible historical provider and SDK combination. Add an explicit dependency/API preflight so preparation failures are reported before the affected tests.

Maintain current transport waits, saved Canvas metadata, read-only action recovery and composer/chat-menu browser checks. Refresh their fixtures and selected client test snapshot without changing the accepted external-agent Settings workflow or application defaults.

releases.title: Set up external agents in Settings
changes: Add, edit and remove external-agent connections in Settings without editing server configuration or restarting the host. Changes are saved privately, take effect for new launches, and detect stale edits.

Choose a saved external agent and an existing workspace in New chat. Keep the remote session binding across reloads; renaming or removing a connection preserves saved chat history and already accepted work.

Keep private launch details out of pickers and ordinary shared observations. Recover a connection save after an interrupted receipt without creating a duplicate entry or repeating the configuration write.

notices.title: Configure only external agents you trust
notices.detail: External-agent setup is now available through Settings and the New chat picker. Existing global connection authority, including Full access, applies; launch commands run as the host service user. Existing chats and defaults do not change. This remains an opt-in text pilot, not a new launcher, voice integration or native-tool parity claim. Removing an entry prevents later sends through it but does not undo accepted work or delete chat history.
notices.action: Use trusted launch commands and private token files, never token contents in configuration or chat. Select an existing workspace for an external chat; create a new chat if the configured launch identity changes. No action is needed for existing native chats.

releases.title: Keep idle chats out of the app update path
changes: Stop treating saved configuration changes in stopped or idle chats as application-update work. App updates wait for actual running work and writer ownership, without asking you to recover unrelated old chats.

Settle verified interrupted configuration attempts without replaying old input; keep saved history, settings and Stop intact. Unverifiable activity is shown as needing attention rather than endless progress.
Prevent an interrupted component preparation from repeatedly waking the updater while it is held for inspection, keeping the app responsive without replaying that preparation.
Read saved conversation views and bundled release notes explicitly as UTF-8, fixing locale-dependent history and settings failures on Windows without rewriting user data.

releases.title: Opt-in external Instance text chats
changes: Pilot a dedicated text chat with one manually configured external Instance. Unified keeps the chat transcript and command receipts while clearly identifying the external agent and its separate execution session.

Support streamed text, Stop, reload and the saved Full access choice for these chats. Full selects permissions offered by the external agent; Ask declines unsupported permission prompts in this pilot. Uncertain delivery is retained without replay.
Simplify update-wait presentation to show the work reported by the host without configuration-recovery groups or reason-versus-chat counts.

notices.title: External chats are an opt-in text pilot
notices.detail: Existing chats and defaults do not change. This release adds no connection-manager UI, voice integration or packaged launcher. External chats do not support native attachments, edit or fork controls. Full can authorize permissions offered by the external agent; Ask declines unsupported permission prompts rather than opening a new permission dialog.
notices.action: Only opt in for an Instance you trust. An operator must configure it and create a dedicated text chat; no action is needed for existing native chats.

releases.title: More reliable runtime preparation and discovery
changes: Improve recovery when preparing shared runtime sources, keeping existing verified generations intact while checking a new one.

Bound Linux discovery checks and their nested Git processes, including cancellation and cleanup. If cleanup cannot be confirmed, retain process custody instead of treating the probe as safely finished.
Maintain workspace registration reconciliation in its own internal owner while preserving existing workspace identities, hidden entries and host-managed selection and history updates.

releases.title: Repair Windows setup downloads and first-use preparation
changes: Windows setup now declares its required .NET Framework 4.8 target so prerequisite downloads use normal Windows TLS defaults instead of legacy compatibility settings. Certificate checks and pinned download hashes remain enforced.

First-use runtime preparation now passes the owned installation directory to private configuration writes, preventing setup from stopping before background-host registration without weakening Windows file protections.

releases.title: A quieter chat history
changes: Successful and cancelled new-chat handoffs now stay under one collapsed Past handoffs row instead of filling the end of a conversation.
Pending, failed and uncertain deliveries remain visible. Check delivery describes opening-brief delivery, not completion of the destination task.
Delivery refreshes and Open chat errors stay visible without resending work or losing drafts.

Prepare the unchanged persistent-computation mechanisms as an independently buildable package. Normal Unified installations still bundle the same runtime; no separate package installation, dependency or policy change is required.

releases.title: Requalify changed component choices without reviving old failures
changes: Keep a verified active component installation separate from source choices changed after its qualification. Updates no longer presents a covered historical source conflict as a new failure solely because the current configuration changed; genuine newer conflicts and incomplete evidence still need attention.

Offer the normal guarded component qualification path when app-level behavior or module declarations change even if their Git branches have not moved. Recheck the captured choices before activation; if they changed again, keep the active installation and retire the unused update intent so a fresh check can qualify the current choices.

releases.title: Maintain output packaging and Appearance regression coverage
changes: Move the unchanged output relationship registry, saved-body decoding and bounded Git-review mechanisms into their independently buildable component home. Unified still bundles the same runtime under the same imports; no standalone package installation, dependency change or output authorization and retention change is required.

Refresh the maintained Appearance browser checks for current profile, gallery and preview controls, preserving read-ordering, stale-response, work-stream, geometry and cancellation coverage. This repairs regression coverage rather than changing the installed interface.

releases.title: Maintain task-transfer packaging and workspace-selection ownership
changes: Move the unchanged signed task-transfer journal and Git-capsule sources and tests into their independently buildable component home. Unified still bundles the same runtime under the same imports and dependency selection; no standalone package installation or transfer-workflow change is required.

Separate the unchanged workspace registration and conversation-selection helpers from Canvas rendering, with callers following their canonical internal owner. Workspace identities, selection effects, history, Canvas visibility and recovery behavior are preserved.

releases.title: Windowless Windows launch, clearer appearance controls and safer saved connections
changes: Add an unsigned Windows preview setup and windowless per-user Start-menu launch, with an owner-logon background host, guarded supervised application replacement and rollback, and data-preserving removal. Foreground launches and task registration alone do not gain supervised update authority.

Give shared notices consistent spacing and contained Undo/close controls on narrow screens. Routine archive confirmations expire only after their navigation has settled, with hover, focus and Keep open preserving the notice; actionable errors and late navigation warnings remain available.

Restore default spinner and activity-dot motion while respecting the device's reduced-motion preference. Keep common Appearance choices direct, with less-frequent controls under Advanced and the device motion setting shown read-only.

Keep legacy OpenAI model-list visibility separate from account binding. Preserve exact saved model choices and deliberate conversation overrides only when their previous connection can be proven; genuine credential, endpoint or source changes and unproven historical visibility edits still require explicit review and save.

Refresh computer-use dependencies to the accepted startup-geometry and approval-loop fixes, preserving selected sources, explicit pins and opt-outs. The application package and each separately prepared worker generation retain their own verified dependency identities; publishing this release does not rewrite existing workers.

Maintenance: the managed Git worktree package now has its own buildable source home. Unified retains the same runtime and imports; no standalone package installation is required. Correct the documented desktop-readiness action envelope.

notices.title: Existing Windows launches do not convert automatically
notices.detail: The Windows setup executable is an unsigned preview. An existing foreground or PowerShell-launched host does not become the supervised owner-logon installation merely by updating the app. Signing and clean-machine acceptance are not claimed; existing data and installation records remain preserved.
notices.action: Use the qualified normal Windows installation handoff before relying on supervised updates. Keep the current healthy host until that handoff is verified. Review any certificate trust request yourself; the installer does not automatically import trust, bypass warnings or elevate security policy. New-installation browser onboarding and sign-out/sign-in verification remain separate delivery checks.

releases.title: Keep lazy worker preparation bound to its saved setup
changes: Preparing a chat from an existing worker generation now freezes the dependencies that were actually prepared, rather than mixing in declarations from a newer app. Inherited baseline identity is kept separate, while fresh component updates still adopt their newly selected setup. Strict installed-graph and package-content checks remain in place.

releases.title: Recover settled configuration holds and preserve current context through tool use
changes: Full-access root agents can discover a chat's retained configuration operation and explicitly abandon an eligible settled operation in the same workspace. Abandonment preserves saved settings and the original receipts; it neither repeats the old write, loads the chat, nor resumes old queued work. Unknown or partial effects remain held.

Keep unchanged current host observations in a stable position during provider tool loops, without keeping superseded authority, memory or images. Real context changes still take effect, and providers remain responsible for native reasoning validity; this is not a guarantee of preserved reasoning across new inputs, compaction or resume.

Use a normal-width navigation sidebar alongside the conversation above the 640-pixel navigation breakpoint when measured space permits. Phone-width navigation stays modal, while Canvas keeps its separate responsive rules and existing drafts and pin preferences are preserved.

Keep permitted file writes usable after unrelated settings changes, with each invocation using one effective writer policy through its guarded engine. Authorized direct independent work no longer needs a connected browser or an unrelated review-count prerequisite; manager-owned commissioning, Stop, revocation and captured child limits retain their existing owners.

releases.title: Choose complete appearances with explicit Global and browser profiles
changes: Choose complete Reference-based appearances from the appearance library, with light, dark and system schemes, accent overrides and coordinated layout, density, detail and execution-display preferences.

Keep Global and This browser as separate complete profiles. Browser edits activate only after storage acknowledgement; reloads and cross-tab changes retain confirmed state. Failed saves keep the last confirmed appearance instead of promoting an attempted change.

Create, preview, cancel, import and export strict format-2 appearance packages. An unavailable selected appearance is reported explicitly and can render Reference for recovery without overwriting the saved selection.
Keep ordinary appearance preference saves quiet, with explicit accent reset and meaningful pending/error feedback rather than routine Saved notices or preference Undo buttons.
Package publishing from its independently buildable component home while preserving Unified's existing imports and POSIX behavior; no separate publishing-package installation is required.

notices.title: Appearance profiles start from a new baseline
notices.detail: This release replaces the earlier theme/profile presentation contract with a new appearance generation. Existing legacy themes, recovered 0.78 format-2 packages and trial profiles/caches remain stored but inactive; they are not automatically converted or applied. A missing new profile starts with Amplifier, system scheme, balanced layout, comfortable density, standard interface/execution detail, all ten execution metrics, all three execution scopes visible, Plan in the composer, decorations on, conversation status off, Appearance as the start view, interim replies expanded and no accent override. Independent valid component placement and view state is retained where compatible; this is not a promise to preserve the previous look.
notices.action: Open Settings → Appearance to choose your look and confirm Global or This browser. Import compatible new format-2 packages explicitly; older stored records are not promoted automatically. Use the explicit reset to remove only an accent override. Keep backups of existing appearance data: old and new versions use different records, and downgrading does not reconstruct or convert the new profile.

releases.title: Make waiting on another chat easier to follow
changes: Keep the waiting status aligned with the conversation and composer. Neutral pending and deferred work now says “Waiting on” with a linked chat name, truncating long names while keeping the full name accessible.
Keep failures, unknown outcomes, decisions and ready results distinct, including when several dependencies are collapsed. Opening a linked chat does not retry or resume its work.
Shorten the sidebar option to “What agents see” without changing its action or position.
Update the repository ownership map and package operations and scheduling from their authored project locations, preserving their existing imports and runtime behavior.

releases.title: Keep fresh work bound to the current saved task
changes: Recognize the current saved task by its verified native identity when a conversation starts a new task after an earlier one completed. Revision numbers from different tasks no longer leave fresh work bound to completed history.

Capture task ownership before preparing child work. Fresh work can retain an already-completed task as history, while completion after assignment, Stop, pause, owner, access and safety checks still prevent stale admission.

Keep rejected or superseded task responses explicitly noncurrent, including when different tasks have equal revision numbers. Preserve their original committed receipts without replaying historical inputs.

releases.title: Keep conversation changes and update recovery consistent
releases.summary: Avoid false interruption after a bundle change and keep component retries explicit, while preserving saved work and runtime checks.
changes: Keep the next turn running when an idle predecessor worker retires during a bundle change. Settle only work owned by the exiting worker, preserving genuine Stop, crash and unknown-outcome evidence. Preserve the exact stopped outcome of confirmed background calls before generic process-loss cleanup.

Keep native-discovered conversations' saved next-message choices valid across restart when their effective working directory and execution revision have not changed. Reuse the existing recording-default identity projection for saved connection choices, and prepare immediate bundle replacements in their qualified candidate runtime graph.

Remove timed replay of failed whole-component preparation and unsupported transient-failure wording. Check does not retry installation; a verified retained target offers one explicit Retry installation action. Changed-input, source, uncertainty and runtime-integrity checks remain enforced.

Use one canonical Foundation source choice for dependency resolution rather than restating its URL in a second override. This is source-policy simplification, not a claim to resolve the historical Mac dependency error.

Put Activity, Send feedback, Automations, What the agents see and Settings together in App options without a divider. Add Copy session ID first in the Chat menu, with truthful clipboard feedback and the requested information icon.

releases.title: Keep saved conversations usable after cache repair
changes: Saved module selections now retain their exact repository revision instead of depending on disposable update-cache paths. Cache reset preserves verified legacy selections before retiring those paths.
Removed the error banner’s duplicate Continue conversation send. Use Retry on a message marked Not sent; use the composer for a new instruction.
Preserved exact source and credential matching for inherited conversations and resumed child work, without repeated Git scans during ordinary checkpoints.

releases.title: Keep next-turn connection checks stable and prepare copied sources once
changes: Fix a false saved-connection verification failure after changing a conversation's model or bundle while provider request recording is enabled. Host-added recording defaults no longer masquerade as account changes; explicit settings and account, credential, endpoint, provider implementation and connection identity checks remain enforced.
Keep recording enabled on the actual provider and preserve saved conversation history and drafts. The repair does not automatically retry failed messages or resolve held configuration operations.

Prepare Git index metadata once in newly copied runtime sources before read-only verification. Keep both full runtime integrity checks, mutation refusal and cleanup ownership. This reduces repeated verification work in new copies, not a promised total startup speedup or a repair of existing generations.

releases.title: Restore the established appearance and sidebar scrolling
changes: Restore the complete established web appearance after the 0.78 visual regression, including desktop sidebar scrolling, reachable navigation controls, execution-row alignment, progress and Stop controls, and composer and attachment layout.

Return Settings > Appearance to complete themes, independent display preferences, and format-1 theme import and export. Temporarily retire Reference-based appearances, Global / This browser profiles, and the new appearance preference actions and format-2 authoring workflow.

Preserve newer saved profiles and format-2 library data without applying, converting or deleting them. A retained valid legacy theme continues to work; where the cutover removed that selection, use the established built-in default rather than claiming to recover it.

Keep the 0.79 startup, idle-update and saved-answer reminder fixes, including explicit restart warnings and exact delivery-state safeguards. Conversations, chat drafts and retained message copies are not reset.

notices.title: Reference appearances and profiles are temporarily unavailable
notices.detail: This release restores complete themes and the earlier display controls. Reference-based appearances, Global / This browser profiles, the new appearance preference actions and format-2 packages are temporarily unavailable while that design is requalified. Newer saved preferences and format-2 library data remain stored and inactive; they are not deleted or converted. A valid retained legacy theme is used, otherwise the built-in default is shown. A personal theme selection removed by the 0.78 cutover is not automatically recovered.
notices.action: Use Settings > Appearance to choose an available complete theme or explicitly reimport a retained format-1 copy. Integrations using the temporarily retired appearance actions must use the restored theme and shell controls from the current action schemas. Do not delete retained profile data to perform this rollback.

releases.title: Restore next-turn setup and simplify update recovery
changes: Fix a next-message bundle startup refusal caused by previewing configuration in a different runtime generation from the replacement worker. Preparation now uses the selected qualified runtime and worker environment while retaining strict configuration checks and Stop handling.

Allow normal application updates when a held configuration operation is idle and exclusive worker absence is verified, without requiring proof of its historical outcome. The hold, saved work and unknown outcomes remain unchanged; active or unobservable work still blocks automatic replacement.

Replace the separate force-restart confirmation dialog with one explicit Interrupt work and restart action. The prepared version and interruption warning are visible before the action; opening update blockers does not authorize a restart.

Clear obsolete delivery reminders for saved answers without checking delivery or sending them again. The answer, provenance and unknown or rejected delivery status remain available in question history. Add the revision- and input-bound question.dismiss action for this workflow.

Preserve validated, payload-free startup exception facts with the exact failed attempt so supported inspection can report more than a generic startup failure. Legacy failures without those facts remain unavailable, not retrospectively diagnosed.

Make the existing scheduling policy independently buildable with its own tests and package metadata. Unified continues to bundle the same scheduling runtime; this changes package ownership, not schedule execution or startup speed.

notices.title: Idle configuration holds no longer prevent app updates
notices.detail: Application updates can now restart normally after current work and worker ownership are proved settled, even when an older configuration operation remains held. Restarting does not reconcile that operation or replay its work. The explicit interruption action remains available for genuinely active work.
notices.action: An installation still running the older updater may need one explicit restart to adopt this repair. After upgrading, inspect unresolved held settings separately; they are not cleared by the update.

releases.title: Separate your look from your personal preferences
changes: Choose Reference-based appearances in Settings > Appearance, with light and dark modes and compatible version-2 appearance packages. Selecting a look does not reapply its suggested personal preferences; suggestions are a separate explicit action.
Keep a Global appearance profile for this service or a separate This browser profile. The first explicit switch to This browser copies the current Global profile; later changes stay separate.

Authorized helpers can request a redacted diagnostic identifying the first failed passive recovery check for an exact held configuration operation. Reading it does not apply settings, retry work or clear the operation. This diagnostic does not observe loaded-state comparisons.

Existing private startup timing reports now distinguish runtime verification before and after preparation. These automatic diagnostic timings add attribution, not a demonstrated startup speed improvement.

notices.title: Choose your appearance again after upgrading
notices.detail: Appearance has been rebuilt. Older appearance, color and display choices are not carried over automatically. Global and browser profiles already saved in this new system are retained. Older custom CSS is ignored, not deleted, and version-1 ZIP packages are unsupported. Older private appearance-editor drafts are not adopted; this does not refer to chat drafts.
notices.action: Open Settings > Appearance to choose your look and review Global or This browser preferences. Authors need to adapt custom appearances to Reference v1 using appearance package format 2.

releases.title: Clearer message progress and recovery status
changes: See source-backed message progress and when a conversation is waiting for your answer, without treating a tool outcome or an idle turn as model success.

Choose optional browser notifications for off-chat questions and approvals. These notifications are off by default. Selecting a notification opens the relevant conversation without answering a question or approving a request.
Restored native history joins message status only when the bounded primary read proves a single matching input; partial or ambiguous history remains unknown.

Saved question answers that are positively rejected before delivery now say they were saved but not delivered. Genuine delivery uncertainty remains unchanged, and no answer is automatically sent again.
Updates separates running or preparing work from configuration recovery holds and shows blocking reasons separately from distinct chats. An update does not resolve held configuration operations.
Repeated identical startup error details are shown once, while distinct diagnostics remain available.

releases.title: Keep conversation checkpoints lighter and update status accurate
changes: Conversation checkpoints avoid materializing the full message history when the context manager provides a checkpoint handle. Existing history-based fallback and recovery checks remain available.

After a verified manual application update, Updates shows the successful current installation instead of an older target-discovery or restart-capability failure. Historical failure details remain available.

releases.title: Reduce repeated checks before conversations start
changes: Preparing a conversation now checks each shared local source only once during the same preparation attempt, reducing repeated scans when several bundles use the same folder.

Source checks skip already-excluded dependency and build folders before walking them. Authored file changes are still checked on the next preparation; source identity and worker ownership checks remain in place.

releases.title: Recover stopped conversations with unfinished settings changes
changes: After a conversation worker has stopped, an unfinished settings change can be cancelled while keeping the settings that were already saved. This clears the stale hold so the same conversation can continue using its saved configuration.
Recovery checks that the saved settings and stopped worker still match. It preserves history and earlier failure records, and does not replay conversation input or uncertain actions.

releases.title: Honor saved component sources when conversations restart
changes: Conversation startup now uses the component sources saved for that conversation, including local repairs and distinct child or named-instance sources. Earlier bundle defaults no longer silently replace these choices.

Required host components keep their supported installed sources, and credential binding and loaded-configuration checks remain in force. Saved conversation history and unresolved recovery records are preserved.

releases.title: Safer recovery and saved conversation choices
changes: Let authenticated Full-access root operators save another own chat's Next message choices and registered workspace defaults through app controls. Bounded readback distinguishes saved choices from active configuration; existing holds, Stop and runtime-control boundaries remain in force.

Retire obsolete mount-freshness markers only after proving that their worker is absent, without clearing the original configuration operation or its recovery fence. Held configuration mismatches now report fixed, value-free section and difference categories.

Keep permitted file-access declarations stable through host-policy intersection, preventing a demonstrated save-and-remount ordering mismatch while preserving the same allowed paths, denials and strict loaded-plan verification. This does not establish the cause or resolution of earlier held conversations.

Recognize independently verified selected-source identities for redundant same-repository sibling mappings in immutable shared storage. Preserve genuine pins and source-policy refusals rather than relying on cache labels or deleting cached sources.

Restore a verified, unchanged prior application generation when a newly promoted update fails its probe. Uncertain recovery retains the safety fence; native macOS cold-start and launchd acceptance remain unqualified.

Resolve native delegate provider identities consistently, including bare module names and exact configured account IDs, using the accepted Foundation repair. Existing conversation runtime environments are not replaced by an app release alone.
Align retained Memory module dependencies with Unified's existing selected Memory source without advancing their module pins, and clarify canonical-client authoring and whole-copy delivery ownership.

notices.title: Full-access operators can save other own chats' future choices
notices.detail: Authenticated Full-access root operators can now save another own chat's Next message settings and registered workspace defaults. This is a saved-choice operation, not permission to Send, stop or restart another chat, replace an active mount, or clear a held configuration operation.
notices.action: Review saved Next message choices and workspace defaults before the next turn. Keep Full access limited to operators you trust with these settings; active work and unresolved recovery holds retain their separate controls.

releases.title: Keep conversation workers recoverable when startup is cancelled
changes: Cancelled worker startup or wake-up now finishes releasing its conversation lock before stopping, so a later worker can continue without waiting for the old process to exit. Saved conversation history and Stop behavior are preserved.

Worker preparation and component updates verify the required shared-session support before opening history. An older retained component generation receives update guidance instead of starting with incompatible ownership handling.

releases.title: Keep saved conversation writes consistent across clients
changes: Use the shared conversation write guard to detect conflicting transcript changes during runtime recovery and checkpoints, preserving saved history.

Check that included components support this protection before starting a conversation or accepting an updated runtime. Incompatible pinned components retain their current state and show update guidance.

releases.title: Keep component updates moving and make returned work clearer
changes: Component updates accept a verified dependency from the same Git source when its development setup also names that same local folder. Explicit source choices and integrity checks remain enforced.
Chats distinguish pending dependencies, returned results awaiting review, and failures, so a manager reviewing finished work is not shown as broken.
