Keep legacy retained-message copies out of the composer while preserving saved text and drafts. Restore clear spacing and wrapping around recovery and restart controls. Keep fresh and empty chats from crashing when there is no dependency activity.

releases.title: Keep long conversations and managers moving
changes: Reduce time spent preparing diagnostic recordings for large model requests by reading known credentials once per recording. Secret scrubbing, image handling and saved-request limits remain unchanged, and each new recording uses current credentials.

Clarify manager guidance to continue through actionable work, return completed deliverables and use the right worker handoff. A progress update alone should not end an assigned task; real Stop, authority and recovery boundaries remain respected.

releases.title: Let waiting managers receive completed work without another nudge
changes: Managers waiting for a worker can receive and review its completed result without a new message from you. Waiting for the same task no longer invalidates its return notification, and receiving a result does not automatically reopen the larger goal. Stop, task limits and changed objectives remain respected.

Conversation activation now uses the shared Foundation runtime owner. Component updates check that the selected Foundation version supports it before changing the active installation; incompatible explicit source pins stay intact and receive a clear refusal.

releases.title: Preserve manual Windows update verification
changes: Keep the exact Windows app update target available for verification after a manual launch, even when a newer release is discovered. This does not reconcile an update target that was already replaced.

releases.title: Reduce delays while saving long-running conversations
changes: Save and publish large execution histories using UTF-8 bytes directly, avoiding repeated wide-text copies when conversations contain emoji or multilingual text. Existing saved history, recovery checks and storage identities are preserved.

releases.title: Safer recovery, coordinated resumption and clearer navigation
changes: Let authorized Full-access root operators inspect and explicitly continue another idle root chat's original configuration operation in the same workspace through app controls, retaining original authority, Stop and sealed-evidence safeguards without repeating a saved settings write or waking the target model.

Find chats through passive title, ID, archive and native-session metadata, then navigate the intended connected client with a client-bound receipt while preserving other clients, drafts and private Settings fields.

Carry an explicit human resume instruction through a single receipt-bound handoff to an interrupted member's existing commissioning owner. The originating root, commissioning owner and named member must all belong to the same workspace. Ownership, Stop, current task and access checks remain in force, and an uncertain admission is not repeated.

Allow normal application replacement around narrowly proven terminal configuration holds without clearing or retrying them. An explicit app-only update supersedes an older whole-update continuation; unknown or partial effects and component activation retain their separate safety gates.

Load file-backed specialist definitions before policy and preparation, including their nested module declarations, while preserving retained plans and child access ceilings. Windows naming-metadata contention remains unresolved; the bounded diagnostic probe is not a fix for that historical failure.

Keep Home in the app header rather than duplicating it in the sidebar, use a chat-plus New chat icon, and make the age filter and first-section spacing more compact while retaining native keyboard and touch access.
Use Work · Amplifier development by default for newly created Amplifier development workspaces. Explicitly saved defaults, custom starters and existing workspaces retain their choices.

notices.title: Full root operators can recover another chat's original configuration change
notices.detail: Within an assigned recovery objective, a current Full-access root operator can explicitly target an original configuration operation owned by another root chat on this installation in the same workspace. Original operation authority, Stop, revision, idle-target and native-evidence checks still apply. Grant editing remains owner-local, and unknown or partial effects stay held. Recovery does not repeat a saved settings write or send model input to the target.
notices.action: No recovery runs automatically on upgrade. Use the supported operation read, reconcile and resume controls for the exact original operation when recovery is needed; inspect retained command evidence after an uncertain action rather than retrying it.

notices.title: Explicit human resumption can reach an existing nested owner
notices.detail: A root handling a current direct human instruction can issue one narrowly scoped resume handoff for a named member to its existing commissioning owner. The originating root, commissioning owner and named member must all belong to the same workspace. The owner must receive and consume that exact handoff in its current authenticated input. This does not transfer ownership, Full access, configuration authority or permission to forward another resume handoff.
notices.action: No interrupted chat resumes automatically on upgrade, and older peer messages do not gain resume authority. Use a fresh scoped handoff for the exact member; preserve newer Stop decisions and inspect the saved admission receipt after an uncertain result instead of submitting another input.

releases.title: Keep saved text and voice messages distinct
changes: Fixed a history display issue that could attach saved text or voice content to the wrong message when a duplicate input contained no text.

releases.title: Recover update waits and manage retained message notices
changes: Resume saved work when its requested app update is withdrawn or superseded, preserving task progress and recovering safely after storage failures or a full inbox.
Hide and reopen the notice for earlier message copies retained in this browser tab without resending or deleting those copies; new unverified copies make the notice visible again.

releases.title: Faster bounded agent state reads
changes: Avoid encoding retained history that will be omitted from bounded agent state previews, while preserving paging, private-draft filtering and immediate visibility of edits.
Share native-history public-content selection while preserving message identities and excluding internal content; no new protocol capability is enabled.

releases.title: Clearer web client ownership and automatic update recovery
changes: Consolidate web client development and testing in their owning components, retiring obsolete frontend copies and duplicate checks.
Resume eligible component updates after their retry delay without requiring another manual check; source conflicts, pinned versions and uncertain outcomes remain protected.

releases.title: Security updates for images and file locking
changes: Update image-processing and file-locking dependencies used by Unified and conversation runtimes to versions containing security fixes. Host image-processing extras and newly prepared conversation runtimes now use the corrected dependency floors.

notices.title: Update existing conversation components for the security fixes
notices.detail: Installing this app release does not replace existing conversation runtime environments. The corrected dependencies are selected when a new runtime generation is prepared; previous runtime generations and their receipts remain unchanged for rollback.
notices.action: Use the normal conversation component-update flow to prepare a new runtime with the fixed dependencies for existing conversations. This release does not automatically update running conversations.

releases.title: Compact sidebar and shared reset recovery
changes: Use compact sidebar controls with a six-stop activity-age slider, including 14 days, and a footer menu for Automation, Activity and Settings. Chat details put the native session ID and copy action before workspace information.

Share one latest successful recovery set between command-line and in-app resets. Older validated successful sets are removed only after the replacement reset completes durably; manual backups and failed, pending or ambiguous legacy attempts are preserved.

notices.title: Successful resets now keep one shared recovery point
notices.detail: Command-line and in-app resets now share a keep-latest policy. After a new reset succeeds durably, older validated successful reset sets are automatically removed, including paired previous-installation copies. Manual backups and failed, pending, unverified or ambiguous legacy attempts are not pruned by this policy.
notices.action: Before another reset, privately copy any older recovery point you need to keep, including its complete paired recovery set, outside managed retention locations. Emergency recovery requires matching reset.py and reset_retention.py files from the same reviewed revision; follow docs/RESET.md.

releases.title: Verified web client assembly and private history text
changes: Build the bundled web interface from verified, independently versioned client source while keeping released installations self-contained and free of Node.js requirements.
Exclude internal and developer blocks from public native-history text while preserving canonical message identities.
Keep media descriptions tied to their canonical messages when using projected public text.
Retry brief Windows file-sharing conflicts during atomic saves, while preserving committed data and reporting persistent failures.

releases.title: Consistent Windows component checkouts
changes: Preserve validated line-ending settings during anonymous Windows component updates so unchanged files are not mistaken for local edits; real edits and pinned sources remain protected.
Add bounded, ordered internal transcript reads without changing recent-history views or enabling ACP history replay.
Align the temporary independent web client source with the already-shipped updater progress behavior; the bundled frontend remains the default.
Preserve original participant text and attachment details in passive history reads when the native input matches uniquely; ambiguous originals remain separate.
Reduce repeated full-history copying during synchronous saves and interrupted-receipt recovery while preserving checkpoint, backup and recovery behavior.

releases.title: More reliable Windows component checkouts
changes: Allow Windows component-update Git commands to use long paths while preserving existing sign-in, proxy and line-ending settings.
Keep the long-path setting scoped to updater child processes; no global Git configuration changes are required.

releases.title: Aligned web client sources and opt-in MCP attachments
changes: Include a verified temporary copy of the independent web client source, aligned with shared activity-age navigation; the bundled frontend remains the default.
Bind browser-test helper processes to the selected server checkout so pairing checks cannot silently use an older installed backend.
Add disabled-by-default support for temporary MCP attachments through the existing execution owner, without persisting their credentials or creating a second connection manager.
Document the optional-integration readiness waiver and the canonical web client source owner.

releases.title: Quieter catalog discovery and lighter activity counts
changes: Stop treating diagnostic folders that never became chats as removed conversations, while still detecting new transcripts and real chat deletions.
Count running, preparing and loading conversations without processing historical attention receipts.

releases.title: More reliable updates and lighter attention checks
changes: Keep eligible component updates moving when an application release check is unavailable, while preserving its warning and pending-update safeguards.
Verify a completed manual Windows app handoff before continuing component updates, without claiming an automatic restart succeeded.
Allow Windows session presentation files to update safely while their ordinary readers remain open, preserving rollback and history ownership.
Reduce work for catalog counts and attention receipts, including SQLite query plans that previously rescanned old receipts.
Retain bounded worker failure diagnostics without exporting private error text or changing retry and Stop behavior.

releases.title: Faster history saves and retained image review
changes: Reduce repeated execution-history encoding across busy conversations while preserving the existing cache budget.
Allow explicit cross-workspace review of exact retained images using existing access controls, including fresh checks before delivery.
Extend automated media checks for native video controls, background playback and keyboard zoom.

releases.title: Shared activity filtering and familiar workspace Chats
changes: Use one Last activity slider in the sidebar or mobile drawer to filter Home, workspace Chats, All chats/search, Recent, Status and workspace chat counts. Pinned chats remain visible regardless of age, and registered folders stay navigable with no matching chats.

Workspace Chats now uses the same Focus, Brief and Studio cards as Home, with one chat toolbar below the workspace tabs. Each workspace retains its own search, status filter, pages and reading position; Work, Files and Details remain separate.

Keep grouping local to All chats while sharing activity age across the attached client's discovery views. Browsing and filtering do not change the open conversation, draft, transcript, runtime or read/attention state.
Reduce repeated validation of unchanged retired accounting receipts during current-work saves while preserving content, owner and publication checks.

notices.title: Activity age now applies across discovery views
notices.detail: The Last activity slider moves to the sidebar and its selected range now also filters Home, workspace Chats, Recent, Status and workspace chat counts for this client. On attach or reload, a previous builtin list's age choice is adopted once; an existing finite choice may therefore hide older unpinned chats in these views. Grouping stays local, pins bypass age, and other clients are unchanged.
notices.action: Check the Last activity range in the sidebar after updating. Choose All to find older chats or chats without a known activity date. Filtering does not stop work, change the selected conversation or mark responses read.

releases.title: Lighter history queries and reliable update identity
changes: Avoid reconstructing unused execution activity during text-only history reads and searches, while preserving message results and browser activity details.
Accept equivalent repository URL spellings during final component-update checks while preserving selected revisions, subdirectories and source protections.
Improve privacy-safe Windows startup diagnostics without exposing paths or message contents.

releases.title: Automatic delivery recovery and safer Windows updates
changes: Check uncertain message delivery automatically after reconnecting, without resending messages or repeating work.
Keep pending messages, drafts and attachments tied to their original conversation and source while acknowledgements settle.
Allow Windows updates to remove read-only Git objects from verified disposable staging copies while preserving real permission and ownership failures.

releases.title: Complete Work history with lighter catalog refreshes
changes: Keep older Work groups reachable through bounded pages, with complete tool details and consistent conversation identities after reopening.
Preserve unchanged tool fields when unrelated records are appended, while still rejecting edited or replaced sources.
Avoid resaving unrelated conversation histories during catalog refreshes while preserving pending progress and failed-save recovery.

releases.title: Reliable Windows component update checks
changes: Avoid rejecting unchanged Windows component checkouts because of line-ending differences, while keeping real source edits protected.

releases.title: Group chats and filter by activity age
changes: All chats, search results and full workspace chat lists can now be grouped by recent date, workspace or status, with the existing sort applied within each group.

Use the keyboard-accessible activity-age slider to show the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, one year or All. All remains the default; pinned chats retain their saved order and remain visible regardless of age while still honoring other filters.

Grouping and age preferences persist for each client's navigation instance. Filters apply across the eligible catalog before paging, without changing the quiet sidebar controls or launching model work.

releases.title: Clearer pinned workspace identity
changes: Pinned workspaces keep a folder icon and a Workspace subtitle, with a separate activity badge, so they are easier to distinguish from chats.

Workspaces with duplicate display names show distinguishing folder context, including aliases and workspaces outside the visible pin list. Full-path display and inspectable, copyable paths remain available.

releases.title: Responsive history reads
changes: Keep agent history list, read and search requests independent of unrelated conversations being refreshed in browsers.
Continue discovering newly created chats while preserving per-conversation history consistency, errors, drafts and execution ownership.

releases.title: Independent updates and faster cleanup
changes: Continue eligible independent component updates when a settled source-download failure can safely retain a verified working revision; keep affected dependencies on their working versions and show which updates were held.
Preserve update failures and avoid repeating an unchanged failed partial update automatically. Unknown operations and unqualified or incompatible combinations remain blocked.
Reduce redundant live-history traversal during resource cleanup while retaining ownership, transaction and cancellation checks.
Add an optional saved-conversation resume boundary for experimental integrations without replaying history or changing execution ownership; full history loading remains unsupported.
Export and verify the canonical shared web build inputs, rejecting linked or nonregular input-lock files before reading them.

releases.title: Accurate Windows command completion
changes: Allow the Windows process guard to finish after a confirmed command exit instead of reporting a false guard failure.
Keep forced cleanup, process containment and bounded shutdown checks intact. This does not enable automatic Windows application replacement or qualify background startup.

releases.title: Reliable qualified updates and execution handoffs
changes: Preserve every package in the qualified component graph when an older application bootstrap needs replacement, including optional transitive dependencies.
Verify a recovered managed browser with the same prepared cache used during installation, while retaining update protection if verification fails.
Recognize equivalent shared-source repository bindings that differ only by the existing .git URL spelling, without relaxing commit, reference, subdirectory or source-protection checks.
Add an optional internal execution adapter with bounded event delivery and explicit unresolved admission and Stop outcomes; existing execution and permission owners remain in control.
Expand paired web-client and resumed-child handoff checks for authentication, history, event recovery, explicit directory pins, saved permissions and fresh-read requirements.

releases.title: Unblock guarded component-update reconciliation
changes: Fix component updates blocked by clean legacy source pins when an included-component update check omits other runtime entries. Fresh validation now checks the full installed runtime inventory before applying the existing guarded reconciliation.

Keep explicit source pins, local or modified checkouts, fork protections and strict source-alignment checks intact. Existing recorded runtime generations are unchanged; this release does not claim that any running installation has completed recovery.

releases.title: Reliable update checkpoints
changes: Keep a conversation’s update checkpoint intact when an idle settings refresh runs, so the app update can finish without losing its worker.
Strengthen internal worker and web-client integration checks while keeping the experimental client packages private and unpublished.
Make the fast release workflow consistent across contributor guidance and release tooling.

releases.title: Workspace names in the sidebar and lighter history saves
changes: Show each chat's registered workspace name beneath its title in Browse, Status, Pinned, Recent and pin-drag previews. The full-path preference still shows paths, long names stay on one line, and standalone managed chats do not gain workspace membership.
Avoid copying already-canonical retired execution accounting again during a current save, reducing repeated work for large histories while preserving saved data, isolation and ownership checks.

Use URI-style separators for installed Git cache subdirectories so native Windows requirement spelling agrees with uv's lock checks. Explicit source selections and existing locks are unchanged; this does not add automatic Windows update support.

releases.title: Clearer connection diagnostics and timely write-access changes
changes: Status reports all verified local listeners and individual failures instead of stopping at the first healthy address. Wildcard listeners enumerate available local interfaces and disclose incomplete coverage; configured public origins are not presented as verified endpoints.

Doctor checks certificate names, validity and local certificate chains, with repair guidance that distinguishes app-owned certificate authorities from missing, expired or supplied certificates. These are local configuration checks, not a claim that other devices trust the certificate.

Approved session write-list changes can take effect at the next supported tool boundary without another message or remount. In-flight tools keep their original policy snapshot; read and denied-path rules, existing child ceilings and Stop remain enforced. Unsupported writer compositions retain the safe retirement fallback.
The update guide now distinguishes accepted requirements for independent, best-effort component updates and minimal interruption from the currently implemented behavior.

notices.title: Saved write-access changes can affect the next tool call
notices.detail: Approved session write-list changes now apply at the next supported tool boundary during active work, rather than waiting for another message. They do not change a tool call already in flight or widen an existing child's permission ceiling. Unsupported writer compositions continue to use the retirement fallback.
notices.action: Review the write paths you approve before saving. You do not need to send another message for a supported active session to use the saved list; use Stop if you need to halt active work.

releases.title: Reliable update waits and Windows source checks
changes: Superseded update waits can be replaced after the original worker confirms cancellation. Late responses cannot overwrite a newer wait; uncertain outcomes remain protected.
Windows worker preparation preserves the checkout’s line-ending interpretation for isolated local source checks, without changing user Git settings or accepting real source edits.
State saves avoid decoding unchanged execution placements while preserving pending-work flags and the existing memory budget.

releases.title: Clearer artifact feedback and safer recovery
changes: Artifact feedback now distinguishes saved content from browser-reported rendering, parse errors, and content that has not been checked. Reports stay tied to the exact revision and client; rendered does not mean visually reviewed.

A direct answer to a saved question can authorize one explicit, guarded continuation of assigned work without resending the question. Stop, access, expiry, draft, and newer-input protections still apply.

Application updates now verify and install the published wheel rather than rebuild from Git. Release identity, checksum, installation ownership, and restart acknowledgement remain required. Automatic Windows replacement remains blocked; installing the prepared candidate requires an operator-verified manual handoff and rollback.
Interrupted reloads of already-loaded chat history now settle on the next eligible load, preserving drafts and saved history.
Browser checks now match the current Canvas and model controls and establish exact editor state before testing cancelled navigation.

releases.title: Safer component updates and faster history reads
changes: Component update checks include selected behavior dependencies while preserving explicit source pins.
Windows worker preparation recognizes native file URLs and long paths without misclassifying clean sources.
History reads used for command admission avoid an extra state save; explicit history loading still reports progress.
Isolated checks refused at the initial environment lock report that no command started. Earlier uncertain outcomes remain unchanged.
Release packages record their exact repository, source revision and version for verification.

releases.title: Lighter progress updates for active chats
changes: Avoid refreshing unrelated Home and navigation views for routine progress in active chats, while still publishing title, status and attention changes.

releases.title: More reliable Windows worker preparation
changes: Write worker preparation and qualification receipts through their explicit owned data root, without weakening private-file checks.
Allow Windows Git operations to handle long cache paths while preserving anonymous credential isolation and leaving user Git configuration unchanged.

releases.title: Safer Windows application update handling
changes: Recognize uv-managed Windows launcher copies only when their installation receipt, private paths and executable bytes match.
Refuse unsupported automatic Windows application replacement before changing the running host, while retaining the prepared candidate and earlier uncertain outcomes.

notices.title: Windows application updates need a qualified manual handoff
notices.detail: Automatic Windows application replacement is blocked before any installed package, application pointer, worker or process is replaced. The prepared candidate remains available; existing uncertain handoff records are preserved. This release does not add automatic Windows update support.
notices.action: Keep the current host running until your installation operator has verified a data-preserving manual handoff and rollback. Restarting the current launcher alone does not install the prepared candidate; do not bypass the update guard or remove source pins.

releases.title: Clearer connection settings and more reliable cleanup
changes: Keep the preferred AI connection label and selector readable at narrow window sizes.
Avoid deferring cleanup when several views share the same large resource graph, while preserving live resource references.

releases.title: More reliable updates and shared execution history
changes: Protected source conflicts stop repeated automatic preparation and show a specific cause; correcting a relevant configuration problem lets normal qualification try again.
Release notes report when details have not arrived instead of loading indefinitely, and display late-arriving notes.
Managed Linux services let the app finish worker shutdown before a planned restart while retaining timeout cleanup. Existing explicit service policies remain unchanged.
Execution preparation reuses compact accounting data across concurrent chats within the existing memory allowance.

releases.title: Keep model choices clear and prepare feedback locally
changes: Save model, bundle and reasoning-effort choices for the next message while active work keeps its current configuration. Different saved accounts, endpoints or provider implementations still block a mismatched connection.

Edit the preferred connection and default reasoning effort without replacing private settings. Conflicting edits preserve another client's newer model choice, and provider default remains distinct from an explicit none effort.

Prepare, preview, copy or save a feedback report locally without GitHub CLI sign-in. Diagnostics are opt-in in new feedback drafts; local reports do not submit issues or upload attachments and excerpts.
Pin menus, update-details navigation and keyboard focus in Recent are more consistent. Failed update checks identify the stage that failed without exposing private error details.

Windows voice diagnostics and update-cache writes use the private app-data boundary. A process-local CPython socket-cleanup backport handles connection resets without changing interpreter files; unrecognized cleanup implementations refuse startup. This is not a general native Windows support claim.
Read-only storage previews no longer acquire the runtime activation lock; actual cleanup still rechecks protection before removal. Unused frontend helper paths were removed.

releases.title: More reliable storage checks and lighter chat counts
changes: Storage inspection can complete while the app is busy, while cleanup still refuses stale reference checks.
Root, child and archive counts avoid sending retained conversation details through count queries.

releases.title: See what shared work is waiting for
changes: A static waiting indicator distinguishes pending replies from an actual Pause, with links to the chats whose replies are pending. Workspace and chat rows are aligned, and the redundant inline workspace pin is removed.
New local managed-test setup recommends Docker Compose. Explicit Incus setups and existing environment ownership stay intact; this update does not migrate or remove retained test resources.

Quiet an old delivery warning with Dismiss warning, then reopen Delivery details when needed. Dismissal preserves your message, attachments and delivery evidence; an uncertain outbox entry remains until exact acceptance is confirmed. Check delivery never resends, stays visible across navigation while pending, and can confirm an exact receipt after the message leaves the visible history window.

Peer messages no longer appear twice after steering history reconstruction. Observation queries avoid scanning unrelated history, and publication reuses unchanged execution projections and their encoded form. Failed terminal status snapshots are retried on a later heartbeat.
Generated images can travel with transferred tasks, preserving their original bytes and edit lineage. Invalid or missing image bodies remain rejected.

Release packages verify the complete prebuilt interface in both wheels and source archives. Release preparation gives clearer next steps, expired unconfirmed deletion previews are cleared, and successful publishing-browser fixtures clean up after shutdown.

notices.title: Docker is the default for new local test setup
notices.detail: New local managed-test setup recommends Docker Compose. Existing Incus configuration, explicit backend choices and retained environments keep their current owner; there is no automatic migration. Registered remote test machines remain Incus-only. This release introduces no new storage format or additional backup requirement.
notices.action: For a new local setup, use the recommended Docker option with an available Docker daemon, or explicitly choose Incus. Keep existing resources on their recorded backend. Use normal Updates to qualify app-managed test components on their target; an app update alone does not replace protected custom component pins.

releases.title: Keep shared work moving as task history grows
changes: Shared tasks now have separate active and history pages, with full details loaded for the item you select. Completed and cancelled tasks remain available without exhausting the assignment's ability to create new tasks; Stop, claims and configured execution limits still apply.
Deleting reviewed shared history now hides only those sessions and their descendants. Other sessions and later work in the surviving workspace stay discoverable, including after restart.

With the updated computer-use component, screenshots are prepared before request fitting and budget attribution. Unchanged requests keep their identity, while a revoked screenshot source is rejected before model completion rather than silently reused.

The updated OpenAI component can report the exact effective model's context window through the existing budget decision. Unknown models and custom endpoints remain unknown. Existing selected OpenAI and computer-use components need the normal component update; an app update alone does not replace protected custom pins.

Frontend builds remove retired generated branding and license files. Successful coordination UI checks clean up their temporary fixture state after graceful shutdown, while failed checks retain evidence.

notices.title: Update custom callers of shared-task actions
notices.detail: Shared-task reads now return bounded summary pages instead of a complete board. assignment.tasks.list defaults to the active view; completed and cancelled tasks are in history. New assignment-control results expose a caller-scoped taskListRef. This is a caller-response transition, not another storage-format conversion; the matching-reader and rollback guidance from 0.65.0 still applies.
notices.action: For custom integrations, follow taskListRef, page assignment.tasks.list with view and nextAfter as after, and use detailRef or assignment.tasks.read with an exact taskId for full content. Pass the same page arguments to assignment.tasks.wait and its version as afterVersion. If coverage.changed is true, refresh to include changes before the cursor. Do not assume one page is the full board, or replace current state with a historical retry's old whole-board receipt. The bundled client is updated; see docs/workspaces/shared-task-history.md for the exact transition.

releases.title: Store shared tasks as individual records
changes: Shared assignment tasks now use individual current-task records, so internal reads can load a task and its declared dependencies without decoding unrelated completed history.

An existing assignment converts atomically on its first authorized task mutation, not on passive reads or startup. Task IDs, owners, claims, results and historical command receipts are retained; an exact retry returns its original result.
The task board response and its 128-item limit are unchanged. Paged task history and removal of that limit are not part of this release.
Work discovery now builds one canonical listing within the remaining request-packet budget, preserving required identities, existing bounds, pagination and explicit unavailability.

notices.title: Back up before the assignment storage conversion
notices.detail: The first authorized task mutation converts that assignment to a new storage format. Older releases refuse a converted assignment when it is accessed. After conversion, use a release that supports the new format. Returning to an older reader requires a matching pre-conversion backup and loses writes made after that snapshot; lossless downgrade is not supported.
notices.action: Before upgrading or allowing conversion, create a full private state backup in Maintenance, wait for it to finish, and retain its archive with the current app version. It contains credentials and is not encrypted. For rollback, stop Unified, preserve the newer app state and shared files, and have the operator restore the matching pre-conversion app state with its older release. Transcript export and the old shared-storage-v1 backup are not a fresh rollback point; ecosystem Rollback does not restore app storage. See docs/workspaces/shared-task-history.md and docs/STORAGE.md.

releases.title: Keep managers and workers moving after completed work
changes: Retire finished workers and readmit available workers using the current saved task state, so completed work does not leave managers waiting on an obsolete activity view.

Fresh peer messages use the recipient’s current saved task before admission. Recover a lost completion reply without repeating completed work, while keeping Stop, task limits and changed-task checks in force.

releases.title: Keep worker creation focused on current work
changes: Avoid scanning unrelated pending messages and retained worker state when an assignment has no open-task limit. Managers can commission work with less bookkeeping; configured task limits and Stop behavior remain enforced.
Let maintainers recover verified frontend build artifacts after an interrupted import, preserving the original build proof and normal release checks.

releases.title: Reduce draft bookkeeping and improve context diagnostics
changes: Avoid unnecessary structured draft checkpoints while typing ordinary text, while preserving quotations and text that needs exact formatting.
Record small, content-free diagnostics when context-budget information is missing, so the remaining cause can be identified without extra model calls or storing conversation content.
Keep readiness package checks accurate as the client asset list changes, while continuing to reject missing, extra or changed files.

releases.title: Prepare native Windows foreground use and clearer runtime diagnostics
changes: Add native Windows foreground support for qualified installations, including private settings, HTTPS browser entry, UTF-8 worker communication and cleanup of owned child processes. Public clean-machine installation and background launch remain experimental and unavailable by default.
Keep saved Work details readable after a Windows file changes, and preserve Stop, history and post-Stop conversation behavior.
Make AI connection discovery follow the exact settings change, so an older response cannot overwrite current connection availability.
Improve bounded worker and export diagnostics while retaining current source, ownership and privacy checks.

releases.title: Recognize client updates reliably and simplify workspace maintenance
changes: Recognize changes across all authored web-client inputs so update and reload discovery uses the correct build identity.
Use consistent workspace and chat page types while preserving the existing list contents, ordering and navigation.
Improve shell SDK packaging and TypeScript support for custom components, clarify appearance-development guidance, and align model-selection browser checks with the current controls.

releases.title: Control retained test output and keep context inspection readable
changes: Choose a cleanup preset in Storage for future temporary test workspaces, while preserving customized policies, retained evidence and uncertain operations. Existing workspace history is not migrated or deleted by choosing a preset.

Opt in to retention for new operation output. Expired logs are clearly marked while outcomes, execution identity and computed results remain available; reading an expired result does not rerun the operation.

Publishing retention can retire eligible local release bodies through the publisher owner. Pins, active readers, resumable work and uncertain cleanup stay protected; remote publications and application installations are unchanged.

Context inspector keeps source text and item lists independently scrollable, preserves selections through resizing and refresh, and shows captured request budgets when the existing provider boundary can verify them. Unsupported attribution stays explicitly unavailable.

Conversation authentication refresh now targets the correct chat. Internal cleanup shares existing error, Canvas and saved-content owners, removes unused panels, and bounds old completed Smart Tool job records without changing running jobs.

releases.title: Continue active work after a verified settings change
changes: An active task can change its own conversation settings and continue automatically after the change is saved and verified. It keeps the same objective, saved progress and remaining work budget, without requiring a separate resume message.

Current tools and delegated work settle before the settings change. Stop, newer instructions and changes to task ownership or permission still take precedence; uncertain earlier effects are not replayed.
Conversation settings show when a task is waiting for this automatic continuation. Updated coordination guidance removes the manual block-and-resume workaround for this flow.

releases.title: Explore conversation context in the Canvas
changes: Context inspector now opens as a resizable Canvas tab with mobile-friendly single-column and wider master/detail layouts. Request and item selection stay in place as you resize or visit other documents.

Known preflight budget evidence is retained across unchanged host request copies. Each limit explains its source or why it is unavailable; model windows are not guessed, and opening the inspector makes no new provider counting calls.
Long source paths move into expandable, copyable provenance so captured text remains readable.
Contributor guidance clarifies autonomous-work goals and contract ownership. This is guidance and design direction, not a new automatic-continuation runtime.

releases.title: Current update status, without old failure chores
changes: Updates now separates current installation health from earlier failed attempts. A verified current component graph no longer inherits red action badges from older source-policy failures; diagnostic history remains available, and incomplete or uncertain updates still need attention.

Unchanged source and configuration conflicts pause automatic preparation until inputs change or you deliberately retry, avoiding repeated copies and dependency resolution for the same blocked candidate.

Component preparation reuses an unchanged policy collection within the same attempt instead of composing it twice. Changed sources, configuration and checked inputs still require fresh verification before installation.

releases.title: One model catalog, with your exact choices preserved
changes: Settings and chat model pickers now share one catalog for your configured connections. Recommendations come from each provider, with clear labels for API results, configured models, static recommendations and simulated models; unavailable or failed discovery is shown honestly rather than replaced by a fallback list.

Saved models and exact model IDs remain usable when recommendation filters hide them. Your selection is not reset to a recommended model, and local recommendations are not presented as proof that an account or service is reachable.

Same-account ChatGPT token renewal no longer invalidates a saved model choice. Account changes, missing credentials and endpoint changes still protect input admission, while Send checks only the selected connection instead of querying unrelated providers.

Model wildcard choices use consistent matching and version ordering across the shared configuration and routing paths. Explicit provider filter overrides remain available where the provider advertises them.
Component updates now accept authored exact dependency pins when the selected and checked revisions match the pin. Different or future commits remain blocked.

notices.title: Model recommendations now follow provider defaults
notices.detail: OpenAI's default discovery recommendations now focus on the GPT-6 family. Anthropic recommends current flagship models, and Gemini recommends current-tier models. Older models or dated variants may no longer appear in the default list. This changes recommendations, not your saved exact selection, and catalog membership is not permission to use a model.
notices.action: Keep your saved model or enter its exact ID if it is missing from recommendations. To change a connection's discovery scope, use an explicit provider model_filters override; an empty mapping {} requests the unfiltered inventory only where the provider advertises that support. The provider still validates credentials, model availability and access when called.

releases.title: Steer supported live model calls and keep conversation recovery moving
changes: An opt-in native model loop lets supported OpenAI models receive corrections while a response is running. The composer distinguishes a sent correction from one accepted or applied by the running model; existing loop defaults stay unchanged.

A confirmed settings rejection before any write no longer leaves the conversation locked behind an unknown outcome. The original failure remains available, and a fresh settings request can recover without replaying the rejected operation.
Desktop approval hooks now reach the actual tool behind Work execution checks. Approved computer actions can proceed, while denied actions and Work restrictions remain enforced.

releases.title: Keep saved-settings recovery stable during component updates
changes: Saved conversation settings can finish verification against the worker that loaded them even when another component update becomes active during that check. Recovery keeps the original saved change and does not replay conversation work.
When a settings change needs recovery, inspection can read the existing worker's actual configuration without starting another worker or reapplying the change.

releases.title: Inspect conversation context and recover saved settings
changes: Open Context inspector from Chat overview to see which categories and items contributed to a recent model request. It separates measured usage from text estimates and shows retained text only when recording settings permit it.

Saved conversation settings can finish recovery after an already-installed component update, recognizing the same configured source choices without repeating the settings change or sending conversation input. Fixed versions and unqualified or changed sources remain checked.

releases.title: Let saved conversation settings finish recovery
changes: Conversation settings can finish recovery when the change was saved but confirmation was interrupted. Resume checks the existing worker, or loads the saved settings if its worker has exited, without repeating the change.

Verified component copies are recognized across runtime generations, preventing unchanged code from leaving a conversation stuck waiting for settings. Stop, permission and uncertain-operation checks remain in place.

releases.title: Leaner context and reliable workspace guidance
changes: Keeps routine app guidance short and makes detailed procedures available on demand through the unified-app skill.
Loads explicitly associated workspace and execution-checkout instructions freshly, without duplicating identical content.
Clarifies current scratch notes, delegated ownership and ordinary recovery while preserving Stop, permissions and existing user files.

releases.title: Reuse finished assignment members without a human relay
changes: A manager with current Full access can explicitly readmit its own unchanged, finished retired member for a follow-up without asking you to relay another instruction. The host verifies the same owner, assignment and saved retirement scope; this does not allow taking over an unrelated chat.

Readmission preserves Stop, completed task history, usage and budgets. It sends no message and does not restart old work; a deliberate new follow-up is admitted separately. Paused, failed, uncertain or changed work remains protected.
Older retirement receipts without the new scope binding still use the existing guarded adoption path. This update does not automatically re-enroll or resume those chats.

releases.title: Let active tasks yield safely for an app update
changes: The new task.waitForUpdate action lets a conversation with an active saved objective finish its current safe turn and wait for one exact staged application update. It preserves the task identity, used budget and already-admitted worker return bindings instead of blocking or pausing the objective.

After the exact healthy replacement is confirmed and its drain is released, the host can admit one guarded continuation. An eligible queued result takes precedence over a duplicate update notification; unrelated conversations and existing tools can finish normally.

Fresh human input, including steering within the same generation, supersedes the old update wait. Stop, user pauses, changed tasks or permissions, uncertain operations and mismatched updates remain protected. The action does not install an update or force a restart.

releases.title: Keep unavailable optional context out of a request refit
changes: When a final pre-send check removes unavailable optional image or memory context, the existing single request-refit attempt now remeasures that reduced request instead of collecting the same context again. This fixes a repeated preparation refusal before the provider call.

The retained request remains bound to the same execution and Work request. Stop, current permissions and final authority checks still apply; there is no additional retry and no replay of sent or uncertain provider calls. Later requests continue to collect fresh context.

releases.title: Save shared work results directly into your workspace
changes: The new coordination.artifact.save action saves an exact authorized retained result into the requesting conversation's working folder, including large binary files. It verifies the saved size and hash, reuses identical existing bytes, and refuses a different existing file instead of overwriting it.

Artifact saves recheck current write access, Stop, execution placement and canonical transfer ownership before publication or reuse. A failure after publication names the destination and retained staging file so the caller can inspect the result instead of blindly repeating the save.

Reduced repeated accounting preparation when publishing updates in conversations with large retained execution histories. Exact history, current task and worker state, and required persistence remain unchanged.

Manager guidance now sends completed review decisions directly to the responsible manager while unrelated work continues, without treating an unfinished staged reply as sealed or bypassing recipient acceptance.

releases.title: Keep routine manager recovery and generated builds moving
changes: Manager guidance now uses ordinary coordination messages for resolved agent-recorded dependencies. The receiving owner verifies the resolution before resuming its existing task; actual Stop, human pauses, unanswered decisions, used budgets and uncertain operations remain protected.

Generated asset rebuilds and verified imports use established source, build and output hashes rather than loading every generated bundle into a conversation. Actual file conflicts and unrelated local changes remain protected.

Added focused macOS packaged-runtime coverage for cold shared-source publication, actual worker readiness and saved-history resume. The verified case uses the published 0.55.0 package with the accepted Foundation revision; it does not claim macOS13 incident reproduction or live-provider acceptance.

releases.title: Let managers hand off fresh work after a completed task
changes: Independent conversations with current Full access can receive fresh direct work from another Full-access manager after completing an earlier objective, without asking the user or a separate coordinator to reopen the chat.

The earlier completion and evidence remain intact, and new work uses the existing native turn allowance. Explicit Stop, paused or cancelled tasks, other managers' commissioned workers, changed access or assignment identity, and exhausted budgets still block admission. Earlier suppressed or uncertain requests are not replayed.

releases.title: Use shared model routing for image generation
changes: New unpinned image requests use shared model routing and permitted ordinary AI connections, independently of the conversation's chat model. The portable Imagegen behavior owns generation, editing and immutable results; missing image support remains visible without preventing ordinary chat.

Fresh conversation plans preserve retained Off choices, paid-call restrictions and explicit account/model pins. Ambiguous or unavailable legacy choices stop rather than silently switching accounts. Existing mounted and saved plans are not automatically migrated.

Image operations retain host admission, cancellation and originating child-run identity. Completed image results preserve bounded routing metadata alongside verified PNG bytes, dimensions, hashes and edit-parent links; metadata is not proof of remote account entitlement.

Image-only connection controls and providers.configureImages are retired. Use ordinary AI connections, model routing and scoped diagnostics; explicit reconciliation removes only a confirmed retained Off preference at its source scope.

notices.title: Image settings now use ordinary connections and shared routing
notices.detail: The separate image-generation setup menu and providers.configureImages action are removed. Existing Off restrictions, paid-call opt-outs and account/model pins remain effective; this update does not delete their saved settings or automatically change existing conversations.
notices.action: Use Settings > AI connections and model-routing controls for new conversations. If diagnostics report retained legacy intent, review the exact scope and use its explicit reconciliation control rather than enabling a different account. Start a fresh conversation or use normal refresh when you intend to adopt the new plan. Image API entitlement is separate from chat sign-in.

releases.title: Reduce repeated history saves during nested tool work
changes: Nested tool actions under Full access now share the enclosing action’s transcript checkpoint even when Work assurance is unavailable. This avoids repeatedly saving the entire conversation between child actions while preserving permission checks, Stop, cancellation and saved results.

releases.title: Keep app updates moving when an optional tool fails
changes: An optional Smart Tool update failure no longer blocks checking for or installing an application update. The installed tool remains available, other ready tools can update, and the failed tool keeps its own Retry and Skip options.

Earlier disk-space and storage-access warnings clear after a later update with the same installed features has successfully prepared and restarted. Diagnostic history remains available; incomplete updates and newer failures still need attention.
Routine release preparation avoids unchanged harness checks and repeated repository-history downloads while retaining package, frontend and native-runtime qualification.

releases.title: Let updates recover after a stopped worker fails to finish cleanup
changes: Updates and explicit Stop can finish cleanup for a worker that has already exited, even if its earlier error reporting or shutdown task failed. Saved failures and uncertain actions remain available, and conversation work is not replayed.
Routine releases use focused frontend smoke checks for version-only changes and reuse the verified build proof; broader frontend coverage runs nightly.

releases.title: Keep stopped conversations recoverable after their worker exits
changes: A new message can start again after a failed conversation’s previous worker has been confirmed stopped. The app clears only that finished worker’s routing state and keeps saved conversation history.
Fresh messages retain their worker identity until they are saved. Uncertain earlier actions and generation-bound corrections are not replayed.
Release checks reuse one prepared runner while publication remains isolated, reducing repeated setup and queue waits without removing package, frontend or native-runtime checks.

releases.title: Reuse prepared test dependencies when only the app version changes
changes: Isolated checks can reuse their prepared dependencies across application version changes, avoiding an unnecessary dependency rebuild. Each check still installs and verifies its own current application source.
Changes to dependencies, dependency source selections, toolchains or test backends still require matching preparation. This maintenance update does not change conversation or tool behavior.

releases.title: Let appearances reflect real activity without distracting at rest
changes: Appearance authors can use documented app-wide active, idle, unknown, unread-attention and disconnected hooks. Activity follows admitted chat and worker lifecycles or real operations; routine metadata reads stay quiet, and reconnects remain unknown until a current baseline arrives.

The optional Night Drive example combines a silver-blue light palette and charcoal dark palette with a slower scanner: eight seconds each way, dark at rest or while activity is unknown. Reduced motion keeps it static; decorations-off and forced colors hide it.
A bounded header-decoration token lets appearances reserve a strip below native window-control geometry without moving controls into that strip. Existing appearances default to no extra space.

Night Drive remains an opt-in source example, not a new built-in or an automatic appearance update. Existing saved library entries and applied styling are preserved; import or apply the updated example separately after installing this release.

releases.title: Repair shared model setup and preserve useful verification results
changes: Shared-runtime model setup now supplies the complete bundle interface, and child-agent inheritance choices survive decision-account normalization without losing account or source validation.

Input diagnostics separate history loading, configuration refresh, worker preparation, admission, reply waiting and delivery publication. These bounded timings help locate delays without recording message contents; they do not claim a speed improvement.

Large Python verification reports can retain complete test identities and diagnostics as lossless compressed JUnit within the existing artifact-size cap. Invalid, incomplete and over-budget evidence remains explicitly unsuccessful.

Focused regression repairs cover current worker and recovery interfaces, complete appearance payloads and quote selection after content readiness. Historical failed checks remain recorded, and the separate scroll-layout issue remains open.

releases.title: Choose how long to keep temporary test workspaces
changes: Storage settings now offer optional expiry for full workspace copies from new queued tests after their environments are removed. The setting is off by default; seven days is recommended when you enable it.

Original source, saved result archives and preservation receipts remain retained. A check can request keepWorkspace:true to preserve its full final workspace; legacy, manual, remote, changed and uncertain copies remain protected.

Expiry verifies exact archive identities outside the application loop and records intent before deleting only the temporary workspace copy. Saved test sizes distinguish an expired copy from its historical size. Files above 8 GiB or verification exceeding 60 seconds per file remain protected.

New test workloads put their default HOME and cache in disposable temporary storage rather than retained results. The directories are created for the workload user and recreated after restart; explicit overrides and complete source/report exports remain intact.

notices.title: Export final work before enabling temporary-workspace expiry
notices.detail: This optional Storage setting is off by default. When enabled, a new queued check's full workspace copy can be permanently deleted after its captured retention period and confirmed environment removal. Original source and saved results remain, but unexported final workspace edits do not. Turning the setting off pauses expiry; increasing the duration extends existing promises.
notices.action: Before a check finishes, save useful final patches, reports and generated results to /artifacts, or submit it with keepWorkspace:true when the full workspace is needed for review. Existing archives are not opted in automatically.

notices.title: Keep test results outside disposable HOME and cache
notices.detail: Default test HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME now use /tmp/unified-test. Temporary contents can disappear after a guest restart and are not part of retained source or result exports. Explicit environment overrides remain supported.
notices.action: Write useful reports, patches and generated deliverables to /artifacts or an explicitly retained workspace path. Use HOME and cache only for disposable state; /tmp retains its existing capacity and execution restrictions.

releases.title: Reclaim unused generated worker environments safely
changes: Existing automatic Storage cleanup now includes verified generated worker environments left behind after their last release reference is removed, using the saved age and size policy. Project source, lockfiles and qualification records remain available.

Current and rollback runtimes, active workers and installers, saved references, modified packages and uncertain environments remain protected. Interrupted retirement and failed completion saves retain their exact recovery receipt without deleting a replacement environment.

releases.title: Keep appearance previews and conversation controls consistent
changes: Appearance cards show deterministic light and dark samples rendered from each theme's actual styling. Reopening Appearance keeps useful choices visible while the catalog refreshes; background appearance reads do not delay Stop or unrelated changes.

Messages received from other chats share ordinary Markdown rendering while keeping their original text, attribution, source links and action boundaries. Delegated-work labels align with their neighboring controls.

Updates uses one consistent status across its headline, details and operation notice. Current retries and unconfirmed restarts keep their own status, while unresolved component attention remains visible until the host resolves the exact occurrence.
Workspace chat counts and activity summaries exclude archived conversations while keeping them available in archive views.
Failure diagnostics preserve the original manager error and operating-system error number when later cleanup also fails, so the secondary failure does not hide the original cause.

releases.title: Clear resolved component update warnings automatically
changes: Recognize when a later verified component update has resolved an earlier dependency-source failure, including after restarting the app. The old failure stays in diagnostic history without continuing to report the installed components as unhealthy.
Keep the complete component list for update recovery, including batches larger than five components. Unrelated failures and incomplete recovery evidence still require attention.

Keep development-only context fixtures out of global dependency overrides, so their source pins do not interfere with component updates. Exact tested dependency revisions remain recorded in the lockfile.

releases.title: Keep nested tool work and component updates moving
changes: Avoid repeatedly saving the full conversation history while one tool program runs several nested actions. The enclosing action still saves the completed transcript, and Stop, recovery and worker-identity checks remain in place.

Component updates no longer treat contributor-only test and development dependency groups as runtime installation requirements. Actual runtime dependencies, explicit source choices and integrity checks remain enforced.

releases.title: Recover a blocked conversation while preserving its work
changes: Trusted callers can explicitly request and inspect context recovery for an idle conversation. The next separately authorized continuation prepares reduced context using the configured model, while preserving original instructions, saved results and uncertain operations.

Recovery must produce a smaller request that fits the existing limits. Interrupted, failed or uncertain recovery stays visible and does not automatically retry, replay work, change models or raise limits.

Recovery remains bound to the same conversation, configuration and Stop boundary across equivalent worker remounts. Changes to accounts, sources, credentials or settings require a fresh valid request.

releases.title: Copy saved file locations and download the version you are viewing
changes: File details in chat cards and Canvas now share clearly labeled full and relative path copying, with the current conversation folder shown. Files saved only in the conversation are identified without inventing a filesystem path.

Download the exact saved version you are viewing, including HTML as a file without executing it. Copying and downloading preserve unfinished preview input, the current selection and your unsent draft.
File controls retain accessible touch targets and restore keyboard focus after closing a narrow navigation or details panel.
Storage cleanup keeps its progress across batches and can recognize unchanged downloaded sources with disposable build copies, while preserving edited, uncertain and active resources.

releases.title: Keep completed checks moving and protect conversation styling
changes: Cleanup can continue after a confirmed storage-space refusal once space is available. A refusal before cleanup starts now identifies the blocking check without falsely reporting a new uncertain removal; earlier uncertain outcomes remain preserved.

The included Digital Rain theme targets the navigation sidebar without also styling conversation quotes and other side panels. Reapply the included theme to use the correction; existing custom styling is kept.
Optional bounded diagnostics distinguish time spent preparing model input from time spent calling a provider, helping locate remaining delays without recording request contents.
Native provider checks now recognize the authorized process-launch path on current Python runtimes while retaining their command and environment checks.
Locked development installs now use the accepted optional decision-provider packages, matching the capabilities already available through normal application installs.

releases.title: Reduce repeated processing in long-running chats
changes: Routine state updates reuse verified saved activity when its contents have not changed, reducing repeated processing in long-running conversations. Changed activity, recovery and storage validation retain their existing behavior.

releases.title: Keep independent workers and visual review moving
changes: Managers can prepare independent workers from an explicit committed source without scanning unrelated retained files. Existing snapshot-based checkout requests remain supported, and uncertain creation outcomes remain protected from duplicate work.

Selected screenshots are prepared together with fewer scheduling waits. Temporary context-read failures preserve an already verified selection while withholding images until current input and permissions are confirmed.
A failed diagnostic test setup now restores its process helpers immediately, so later checks are not affected by leftover test mocks.

releases.title: Give managers independent workers and keep shared context current
changes: Managers can commission many independent workers with a saved objective and a clean isolated source checkout before the first working turn. Existing creation receipts preserve ownership through restart and prevent duplicate initial work.

Workspace starters and coordination guidance favor complete deliverables, ordinary repair and focused validation within the assigned objective, and result review without routine acknowledgment turns. Shared scratch stays a short current index; detailed history and recovery instructions are read when needed.

Full-access requests retain the same authority behavior when their input needs refitting. Required native input, Stop and permission checks remain in force; refused requests retain clearer bounded diagnostics.
Fresh scheduled tasks preserve explicitly disabled agents. Release checks also retain clearer browser, attachment and cleanup failure evidence.

releases.title: Use saved decision models and verify browser form controls
changes: Jev and local decision connections added in Settings now use their canonical adapter sources, so configured accounts can start without re-entering credentials or silently falling back because a source was missing. Explicit source choices remain preserved.

Browser observations include checkbox and radio states. Form verification checks every requested value, distinguishes mixed or unknown states, and rejects stale toggle actions and invalid completion conditions before input.
Amplifier Connect 0.2.3 adds the same checked-state observations for connected browsers while preserving its extension identity, pairing and permissions.

notices.title: Update Amplifier Connect for checkbox verification
notices.detail: Connected-browser checkbox and radio verification requires Amplifier Connect 0.2.3. The managed browser receives the correction with the server update. Existing pairing and permissions stay unchanged.
notices.action: For an existing unpacked extension, stop browser access, replace its files with version 0.2.3, and reload the same extension. Then select the intended tab again. Do not remove or pair the extension again.

releases.title: Show saved decision connections promptly and reduce sidebar delivery waits
changes: Saving or removing an AI connection now refreshes its decision-model choices in the same result. Setup confirms the saved connection immediately, with clear loading and retry states if optional choices cannot be refreshed.

Reduce repeated scheduling waits when returning sidebar and history query results on a busy server. Preserve saved history, cancellation and freshness checks, and retain clearer diagnostics when a read cannot finish.
Correct isolated browser and agent fixtures so release verification recognizes their owned helpers and current interaction controls.

releases.title: Connect decision models and choose browser and computer use together
changes: Installed decision providers now offer direct account setup instead of sending you back to Updates. Installing support still does not connect an account or change your selected model.
Choose the same decision model for browser and computer use in one save, with explicit consent, or configure each separately. Editing one preserves the other and your ordinary chat connections.
Retire an earlier browser installation warning only after a verified browser launch and confirmation of the exact restarted installation. Unrelated and newer failures remain available for review.

releases.title: Finish installing optional browser and decision support
changes: Fix optional browser and decision support installation omitting required dependencies when the same tool was already installed without those features. Existing package versions and source choices remain preserved.
Validate the complete prepared installation before activating it. If installation cannot be completed, the current app remains available and the failure stays inspectable.

releases.title: Use browsers from your chats, with optional decision models
changes: Work chats can use a managed browser or a browser you connect, with a live view, explicit target selection and controls to stop access or take over.
Keep your ordinary chat model for browser tasks, or explicitly choose a supported decision model through your saved AI connection. Installing decision support does not change your selected model.
Browser setup and recovery explain missing optional components and preserve saved accounts and device permissions. Installing support does not enroll a device or enable access.
Connected-browser delivery rechecks permission and the selected page before returning screenshots, and recovers saved operation results without repeating uncertain actions.

releases.title: Delete managed chats with worker history
changes: Fix Delete chat rejecting a valid managed conversation because one of its delegated workers has a different kind of session ID. The reviewed deletion includes the conversation’s owned worker history, saved captures and runtime records.

Keep ownership, active-work and transfer safeguards in place, and release acquired locks even when a deletion attempt is cancelled or cleanup reports another error. Workspace chats can still be archived; this does not expand which chats are eligible for deletion.

releases.title: Keep inline previews in place after reloading
changes: Reloading the app preserves your choice to show an artifact inline or as a saved card, while preparing fresh executable content for the selected version.
Update the bundled content sanitizer, validation library and frontend build tooling to address reported dependency security advisories.
Improve release verification: retain bounded logs and partial results when a Python check cannot finish, and correctly distinguish queued peer notifications from model activity in the browser checks.

releases.title: Keep conversations moving when an unsent request needs refitting
changes: Avoid incorrectly stopping a conversation with an authority-change error when a slow saved-image check requires an unsent model request to be prepared again. Reuse that request’s captured context, then confirm current work permissions immediately before sending.
Preserve Stop, cancellation, changed-input and changed-permission checks. Unavailable permission information remains a distinct refusal; previously sent work is not retried automatically.

releases.title: Clearer scheduled-task diagnostics and inherited workspace defaults
changes: When a scheduled new task's configuration changes between conversation creation and task admission, retain a safe comparison of configuration hashes and changed categories. Stop, permission and configuration guards remain strict; no task is replayed automatically.

New Amplifier development workspace plans inherit an explicitly saved app or shared bundle default without pinning that choice in project settings. With neither saved, the starter keeps its anchors-amp-dev fallback. Existing workspaces, chats, custom starters and reviewed revision-5 plans remain unchanged.

notices.title: New Amplifier development plans can inherit your saved default
notices.detail: New plans now inherit an explicitly saved Unified app or shared Amplifier bundle default. Without one, the starter retains anchors-amp-dev. Existing workspaces and chats are not migrated, and already reviewed plans keep their recorded choice.
notices.action: Review the bundle choice when preparing a new workspace. To pin a different bundle, duplicate the starter and set an explicit workspace bundle default before preparing the plan.

releases.title: A new appearance, deliberate Canvas loading and clearer recovery
changes: Add Breadbin, an optional home-computer-inspired appearance with light and dark palettes. No appearance is selected automatically or saved copy replaced. Shared transcript fades now stay visible during pointer-based question review while protecting keyboard focus, editing and active embedded reviews.

Keep a running Canvas preview on its loaded definition when newer content arrives. Refresh checks for changes; an explicit Load action changes the running preview, with dirty-state and uncertain-response safeguards.
Track unresolved update failures by cause and occurrence. Let users explicitly acknowledge supported historical uncertainty without claiming recovery, clearing current errors or replaying an update.

Interpret omitted Git refs consistently with Foundation's main default while preserving explicit refs, protected-source checks and exact commit verification. Report missing or conflicting source bindings without mislabeling them as local edits.
Apply the existing durable-checkpoint policy when a managed context uses its default Boundary engine, preserving explicit checkpoint opt-outs and unsupported-engine rejection.

Include the selected-model request recovery from 0.45.8: remeasure once when prepared image checks change before sending, while preserving model settings, Stop and authority checks without repeating completed tools.

Allow corrections to a worker's staged report in the same turn, keeping earlier reports and files inspectable. Managers can resume an interrupted commissioned worker from a fresh human instruction only after the host confirms its previous generation and native worker have stopped; prior outcomes, Stop and permission checks remain in force.

Let ordinary Python import caches stop blocking retirement of otherwise verified, unused runtime copies, while preserving changed source and unknown files. Keep test-environment cleanup recoverable when a confirmed failure occurs before its helper starts; retain the failed request and never treat an uncertain removal as safe to repeat.

Retain larger files in new worker handoffs and integration results using chunked snapshots and verified downloads. Available disk space still limits retention; text previews stay bounded, and saved bytes do not prove correctness or repair older failed captures.

Apply the unused-copy size target across previously measured cleanup batches, with fresh checks before removal. Show the rolling estimate separately from the current inspection; it is not a complete disk inventory. Batch background resource inspection to reduce per-file scheduling while retaining reference and cancellation checks.

Allow a new cleanup attempt for an interrupted local Docker removal only after fresh checks confirm the original owner is stopped and its local executor has settled. Preserve the old unknown receipt and export the current files again before teardown.
Reduce repeated receipt copying during conversation saves while preserving accounting history and independent mutable values.

notices.title: Refreshing a running preview no longer replaces its definition
notices.detail: A running HTML or Babylon preview can remain on its loaded version while Canvas reports newer saved content. Refresh is a read, not permission to replace the active preview.
notices.action: Use Load when you want the newer definition. Review any unsaved-state warning before replacing the running preview.

releases.title: Keep selected-model conversations going after image checks change
changes: Apply the existing one-time request recovery to conversations with an explicitly selected model, including managers. If an image check changes before the model request is sent, Amplifier measures the updated request again while preserving the chosen model and reasoning settings.

Completed tools are not repeated. Stop, newer input, changed permissions and uncertain provider outcomes still prevent automatic recovery. Conversations that already stopped need an explicit continuation.

releases.title: Keep saved results and recovery from blocking ongoing work
